§3 Local syntomic computations (3.1 local complexes, 3.2 change of disk, 3.3 (ϕ,∂)- and (ψ,∂)-modules, 3.4 change of annulus, 3.5 change of Frobenius, 3.6 syntomic and de Rham cohomology)

§4 Syntomic cohomology and (ϕ,Γ)-modules (4.1 forms to Koszul complexes, 4.2 group cohomology and Koszul complexes, 4.3 (ϕ,∂) to (ϕ,Γ), 4.4 change of annulus, 4.5 change of disk, 4.6 passage to Galois cohomology, 4.7 comparison with the local Fontaine–Messing map)

summary: Partial extraction of the integral log-syntomic/nearby-cycle comparison and its semistable applications. Independent review corrects source formulas, invalid broad planned claims, dependency cycles and provenance, but rejects the ten route drafts pending shared ownership, source-qualified splitting, all definition APIs/tests and recursive proof closure. Existing proper formal semistable comparison belongs to CohomologyComparisons:CP.4.
conventions: Locators are the statement numbers of the authors' version together with its page numbers (68 pages; the published pagination in Invent. math. 208 is 1–108 and was not accessible). The paper's basic currency is Definition 1.13: a map of Z_p-modules is p^N-injective (resp. p^N-surjective) if its kernel (resp. cokernel) is annihilated by p^N, and p^N-quasi-isomorphism, p^N-exact and p^N-acyclic are defined in the same way; every comparison below is of that kind and source bounds and independently justified replacements are distinguished, since the whole point of the paper is to control it. Brackets are homotopy limits: [C --f--> C′] := holim(C → C′ ← 0), and a bracketed commutative square means the homotopy limit of the two rows; the paper notes that these squares are strictly commutative, so that the total complex of the double complex may be used, everywhere except in §5. K is a finite totally ramified extension of F = W(k)[1/p] of degree e with uniformiser ϖ and Eisenstein minimal polynomial P = P_ϖ(X_0); i(K) is the largest n with ζ_{p^n} ∈ K, e_0 = [F_{i(K)}:F], f = e/e_0, δ_K = e·v_p(d_{K/F_{i(K)}}) and δ_R = ⌈δ_K/f⌉; 'K contains enough roots of unity' means δ_K + [K:F_{i(K)}] < e/(2p), which implies δ_R + 1 ≤ e_0/(2p), not the strict rounded inequality (E25). The radii are u = (p−1)/p and v = p−1 for p ≥ 3, u = 3/4 and v = 3/2 for p = 2. Two Frobenii are in play and differ only on the arithmetic variable: ϕ_Kum with ϕ_Kum(X_i) = X_i^p, which computes crystalline and syntomic cohomology, and ϕ_cycl, the Frobenius of (ϕ,Γ)-module theory, which is defined only after assuming enough roots of unity and only with values in R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ. The Frobenius on differential forms is divided: it acts coefficientwise in the basis of the ω_j, so the natural Frobenius on Ω^i is p^i·ϕ, which is why the powers p^• appear in the complexes. Z_p(r)′ := (1/p^{a(r)})Z_p(r) for r = (p−1)a(r) + b(r) with 0 ≤ b(r) ≤ p−1 (an ambiguous endpoint convention requiring resolution, E31) is the source’s twist in which the Fontaine–Messing map is integrally defined. In §§2.4–2.6 the paper writes A_R, E_R, G_R = Gal(R̄/R) with R̄ the maximal extension of R unramified outside the divisor at infinity after inverting p, while in §2.5.3 it also writes A^deco_R for the image of R^deco_ϖ under ι_cycl: the items below distinguish the two by writing A^deco_R̄ for the period ring and A^deco_R for the image.

items.name: Arithmetic setup for the local comparison
items.statement: O_K is a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field K of characteristic 0 and perfect residue field k of characteristic p; O_F = W(k) and F = O_F[1/p], so that K is a totally ramified extension of F of degree e = [K:F], the absolute ramification index. O_K̄ is the integral closure of O_K in an algebraic closure K̄, G_K = Gal(K̄/K), and ϕ = ϕ_{W(k)} is the absolute Frobenius of W(k). For a log-scheme X over O_K, X_n denotes its reduction mod p^n and X_0 its special fibre. ϖ denotes a uniformiser of O_K and P = P_ϖ(X_0) ∈ O_F[X_0] its minimal (Eisenstein) polynomial over F.
items.note: The standard local setup; the atlas builds the period-ring and local-field interfaces at PadicHodgeTheory R06.1.

items.name: Semistable chart and the log structure
items.statement: X is a fine and saturated log-scheme, log-smooth over O_K with the log structure coming from the closed point; X_tr is the locus where the log structure is trivial, an open dense subset of the generic fibre. X has semistable reduction over O_K, or is a base change of such a scheme over the ring of integers of a subfield of K, when locally X = Spec(A) for A étale over O_K[X_1^{±1},…,X_a^{±1},X_{a+1},…,X_{a+b},X_{a+b+1},…,X_d,X_{d+1}]/(X_{d+1}X_{a+1}···X_{a+b} − ϖ^h), 1 ≤ h ≤ e. With D := {X_{a+b+1}···X_d = 0} ⊂ Spec(A) the log structure on Spec A is the one associated to the special fibre and to the divisor D, and Spec(A)_tr = Spec(A_K) ∖ D_K.
items.note: CR.5 builds fs log structures, charts and the standard semistable chart O_K[x_1,…,x_d]/(x_1···x_r − π); this is that chart with a horizontal divisor at infinity and a power ϖ^h.

items.name: The modified Tate twist Z_p(r)′
items.statement: For r ≥ 0 write r = (p−1)a(r) + b(r) with 0 ≤ b(r) ≤ p−1, and set Z_p(r)′ := (1/p^{a(r)})·Z_p(r) ⊂ Z_p(r) ⊗ Q_p; the finite-level sheaves Z/p^n(r)′ are defined in the same way. This is the twist in which the Fontaine–Messing period map is integrally defined. The printed endpoint interval does not select a unique pair; this is a parameterized lattice until E31’s normalization obligation is resolved.

items.name: The log-syntomic sheaf S_n(r)_X
items.statement: For r ≥ 0, S_n(r)_X is the (log) syntomic sheaf modulo p^n on X_{0,ét}: the derived Frobenius and filtration eigenspace of log-crystalline cohomology, that is the mapping fibre of p^r − ϕ on the r-th filtration step of the log-crystalline complex, equivalently a relative Fontaine functor. Its cohomology is log-syntomic cohomology, H^i_syn(X,r).
items.note: D.2 constructs a syntomic mapping fibre from filtered de Rham complexes and Frobenius data in the smooth unramified setting; the logarithmic and integral form used here is what this paper needs. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: The Fontaine–Messing–Kato period morphism
items.statement: For i : X_0 ↪ X the special fibre and j : X_tr ↪ X the open immersion, Fontaine–Messing and Kato construct period morphisms α^FM_{r,n} : S_n(r)_X → i^*Rj_*Z/p^n(r)′_{X_tr} for r ≥ 0, from logarithmic syntomic cohomology to logarithmic p-adic nearby cycles.
items.note: Quoted from Fontaine–Messing [28] and Kato [36]; the paper's task is to prove it is a quasi-isomorphism after truncation. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Theorem 1.1(i): the period map is a quasi-isomorphism up to p^{Nr+c_p}
items.statement: For 0 ≤ i ≤ r consider α^FM_{r,n} : H^i(S_n(r)_X) → i^*R^ij_*Z/p^n(r)′_{X_tr} (1.2). If K has enough roots of unity then the kernel and cokernel of this map are annihilated by p^{Nr+c_p}, for a universal constant N — not depending on p, X, K, n or r — and a constant c_p depending only on p (and on d if p = 2).

items.name: Theorem 1.1(ii): the general case
items.statement: In general (no assumption on the roots of unity in K), the kernel and cokernel of α^FM_{r,n} : H^i(S_n(r)_X) → i^*R^ij_*Z/p^n(r)′_{X_tr} for 0 ≤ i ≤ r are annihilated by p^N for an integer N = N(e,p,r) depending on e, p and r but not on X or n.
items.note: Deduced from Theorem 1.6 (the case with enough roots of unity) by a descent argument, §5.1.

items.name: The classical small-twist isomorphism
items.statement: For i ≤ r ≤ p−1 the period map α^FM_{r,n} : H^i(S_n(r)_X) ≅ i^*R^ij_*Z/p^n(r)_{X_tr} is an isomorphism (no constants, and the unmodified twist), for X log-smooth over a henselian discrete valuation ring O_K of mixed characteristic. Kato, Kurihara and Tsuji; Tsuji also generalised it to some étale local systems.
items.note: Quoted from [35], [36], [40], [63], [64], [62]; the statement this paper generalises to all r at the cost of universal constants. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: The syntomic exponential α_{r,i}
items.statement: For X a quasi-compact formal semistable scheme over O_K (for example a semistable affinoid) and i ≥ 1, α_{r,i} is the composition H^{i−1}_dR(X_{K,tr}) → H^i(X,S(r))_Q --α^FM_r--> H^i_ét(X_{K,tr},Q_p(r)). For a proper semistable scheme X over O_K and 1 ≤ i ≤ r−1 it is the Bloch–Kato exponential D_dR(V_{i−1}) → H^1(G_K,V_{i−1}) = H^i_ét(X_K,Q_p(r)) for V_{i−1} = H^{i−1}_ét(X_K̄,Q_p(r)).
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators:L1 owns the local-field Bloch–Kato exponential; D.2 does not own this general semistable formal-scheme map. The whole item remains missing.

items.name: Corollary 1.4: a generalised Bloch–Kato exponential isomorphism
items.statement: For i ≤ r−1 the map α_{r,i} : H^{i−1}_dR(X_{K,tr}) → H^i_ét(X_{K,tr},Q_p(r)) is an isomorphism. The map α_{r,r} : H^{r−1}_dR(X_{K,tr}) → H^r_ét(X_{K,tr},Q_p(r)) is injective, but its cokernel can be very large if dim X_K ≥ 1.
items.note: Proved as Corollary 5.11; it follows from Theorem 1.1 together with the easy comparison between de Rham and syntomic cohomology (Lemma 3.14, Corollary 3.16).

items.name: Enough roots of unity
items.statement: A condition on K, defined in §2.2.1: it is what makes the cyclotomic embedding and the element π_K of the field-of-norms theory available. For any K the field K(ζ_{p^n}) contains enough roots of unity as soon as n ≥ c(K) + 3, where c(K) is the conductor of K.
items.note: The hypothesis of Theorem 1.6 and of Theorem 1.1(i); Remark 1.7 explains how to remove it at the cost of constants depending on K.

items.name: Theorem 1.6: the local Lazard comparison
items.statement: Let R be the p-adic completion of an étale algebra over R_□ := O_K{X_1^{±1},…,X_a^{±1},X_{a+1},…,X_{d+1}}/(X_{d+1}X_{a+1}···X_{a+b} − ϖ), with the log structure induced by the divisor at infinity X_{a+b+1}···X_d = 0 and the special fibre, and let G_R = Gal(R̄/R) for R̄ the maximal extension of R unramified outside that divisor after inverting p. If K contains enough roots of unity then the maps α^Laz_r : τ^{≤r}Syn(R,r) → τ^{≤r}RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)) and α^Laz_{r,n} : τ^{≤r}Syn(R,r)_n → τ^{≤r}RΓ_cont(G_R,Z/p^n(r)) → τ^{≤r}RΓ((Sp R[1/p])_{tr,ét},Z/p^n(r)) are quasi-isomorphisms up to p^{Nr}, for a universal constant N.
items.note: The first main result: more precise than Theorem 1.1 because no étale localisation is required. Proved in §4 (Theorem 4.14) with the identification of α^Laz and α^FM in Theorem 4.16.

items.name: Remark 1.7: removing the roots-of-unity hypothesis
items.statement: The descent argument of §5.1 would also remove the hypothesis that K contains enough roots of unity from Theorem 1.6, at the cost of constants depending on K; the authors expect that the constants can be made to depend only on the valuation of the different of K. They also expect an analogue of Corollary 1.4 for a general affinoid algebra smooth in characteristic 0, with constants depending on the p-adic valuation of suitable Jacobians (the 'defect of smoothness in mixed characteristic'), using the purity theorems to pass to a finite cover of very small defect.
items.note: An expectation, not a theorem: a design job must not plan it as one. Recorded under gaps.

items.name: The base-changed comparison and its rational form
items.statement: Theorem 1.1 holds also for base changes of semistable schemes, which gives a quasi-isomorphism up to p^{Nr} for a universal constant N: α^FM_{r,n} : H^i(S_n(r)_{X_{O_K̄}}) → i^*R^ij_*Z/p^n(r)′_{X_{K̄,tr}} for i ≤ r, where i : X_{0,k̄} ↪ X_{O_K̄} and j : X_{K̄,tr} ↪ X_{O_K̄} (1.8); hence an isomorphism α^FM_r : H^i_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q ≅ H^i(X_{K̄,tr},Q_p(r)) for i ≤ r (1.9).
items.note: Recovers Tsuji's [63, Theorem 3.3.4]; (1.9) is the input to the syntomic proof of the semistable comparison theorem.

items.name: Corollary 1.10: the semistable conjecture for formal schemes
items.statement: Let X be a proper semistable formal scheme over O_K. There exists a natural B_st-linear, Galois-equivariant period isomorphism α : H^i(X_{K̄,tr},Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_st ≅ H^i_HK(X) ⊗_F B_st preserving the Frobenius and the monodromy operators, which induces a filtered isomorphism α : H^i(X_{K̄,tr},Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X_{K,tr}) ⊗_K B_dR.
items.note: The second main result, proved as Corollary 5.21/5.26. The novelty is the method: no Poincaré duality is used, which is what allows the passage from schemes to formal schemes.

items.name: p^N-isomorphisms and p^N-quasi-isomorphisms
items.statement: For N ∈ N and f : M → M′ a morphism of Z_p-modules, f is p^N-injective (resp. p^N-surjective) if its kernel (resp. its cokernel) is annihilated by p^N, and a p^N-isomorphism if it is both. In the same way one defines a p^N-exact sequence, a p^N-acyclic complex (one whose cohomology groups are annihilated by p^N) and a p^N-quasi-isomorphism: a map in the derived category inducing a p^N-isomorphism on cohomology.
items.note: The paper's basic currency: almost every comparison in it is a p^N-quasi-isomorphism, and the exponent is tracked throughout. A formalisation needs this as a definition with its calculus (composition, cones, spectral sequences), not as an informal 'up to constants'.

items.name: The homotopy-limit shorthand
items.statement: For f : C → C′ a map in the dg derived category of an abelian category, [C --f--> C′] := holim(C → C′ ← 0); and for a commutative square with rows C_1 --f--> C_2 and C_3 --g--> C_4, the bracket notation means [[C_1 → C_2] → [C_3 → C_4]]. When the square is strictly commutative this is the total complex of the associated double complex; in this paper that is the case everywhere except in §5.
items.note: The exception in §5 matters: the squares there are only commutative in the derived category, so the total-complex model is not available and the homotopy limit must be used.

items.name: The chain of comparisons proving Theorem 1.6
items.statement: The proof of Theorem 1.6 is the composition of the following comparisons, each a p^{Cr}-quasi-isomorphism for an absolute constant C: Syn(R,r) ≃ Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) ≃_{τ^{≤r}} Kum(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) (change of disk and annulus of convergence, §§3.2 and 3.4); ≃ Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) (change of Frobenius from ϕ_Kum to ϕ_cycl, §3.5); ≃ Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rA^{[u,v]}_R) (differential forms to Koszul complexes, §4.1); τ^{≤r}Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rA^{[u,v]}_R) ≃ τ^{≤r}Kos(ϕ,Lie Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) (removing the filtration by multiplying by powers of t — the only place where truncation is unavoidable); ≃ Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) (Lazard, §4.2); ≃ Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{(0,v]+}_R(r)) ≃ Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A_R(r)) (§§4.4–4.5, by the ψ operator and acyclicity of the ψ = 0 eigencomplex); ≃ [RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_R(r)) --1−ϕ--> RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_R(r))] ≃ [RΓ_cont(G_R,A_R̄(r)) --1−ϕ--> RΓ_cont(G_R,A_R̄(r))] ≃ RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)) (§4.6, by decompletion and the relative Artin–Schreier sequence). Finally the p-adic K(π,1)-lemma and Abhyankar's lemma identify RΓ_cont(G_R,Z/p^n(r)) with RΓ((Sp R[1/p])_{tr,ét},Z/p^n(r)).
items.note: The architecture of §§3–4. Each step is an item of its own below; this item records the composite and the order, which is what a design job must reproduce.

items.name: The Banach-Space argument for the semistable conjecture
items.statement: To prove Corollary 1.10 one shows the long exact sequence → (H^{i−1}_dR(X_{K,tr}) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r → H^i_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q → (H^i_HK(X) ⊗_F B^+_st)^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} → (H^i_dR(X_{K,tr}) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r → (1.12), which for i < r gives short exact sequences 0 → H^i_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q → (H^i_HK(X) ⊗_F B^+_st)^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} → (H^i_dR(X_{K,tr}) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r → 0. The surjectivity is proved by finite-dimensional Banach Space theory: f_i is the evaluation at C = K̄^∧ of a map of finite dimensional Banach Spaces, H^i_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q is a finite dimensional Q_p-vector space by (1.9) and Scholze's finiteness, so Coker f_i has Dimension (0,d_i), while (H^i_dR ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r is a successive extension of C-vector spaces; a map from such a Space to a Dimension-(0,d) Space is zero, so Coker f_i = 0. With the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism the pair (H^i_HK(X), H^i_dR(X_{K,tr})) is then a (ϕ,N)-filtered module, a weight argument gives V_st(H^i_HK,H^i_dR) ≅ H^i(X_{K̄,tr},Q_p) and a dimension count gives t_N = t_H, whence weak admissibility.
items.note: The second architecture: §5.2 carries it out. The point of method is that Poincaré duality is replaced by the Dimension calculus of Banach Spaces.

items.name: Convergent power series over a topological ring
items.statement: For a topological ring Λ, Λ{Z} with Z = (Z_1,…,Z_s) is the ring of power series Σ_{k∈N^s} a_kZ^k with a_k ∈ Λ tending to 0; for a continuous λ : Λ_1 → Λ_2 and F ∈ Λ_1{Z}, F_λ ∈ Λ_2{Z} is obtained by applying λ to the coefficients. For Λ′_1 = Λ_1{Z}/(Q) with Q = (Q_1,…,Q_s), extending λ to Λ′_1 amounts to solving Q_λ(Y) = 0 in Λ_2; J := (∂Q_j/∂Z_i)_{1≤i,j≤s} ∈ M_s(Λ_1{Z}).

items.name: Proposition 2.1: an implicit function theorem
items.statement: Let λ : Λ_1 → Λ_2 be continuous and Λ′_1 = Λ_1{Z}/(Q). Suppose there are z ∈ Λ_2, an ideal I of Λ_2 with z^{−2}I ⊂ Λ_2 and Λ_2 separated and complete for the z^{−2}I-adic topology, Z_λ ∈ Λ_2^s and H_λ ∈ z^{−1}M_s(Λ_2), such that the entries of Q_λ(Z_λ) lie in I and those of H_λJ_λ(Z_λ) − 1 lie in z^{−1}I. Then Q_λ(Y) = 0 has a unique solution in Z_λ + (z^{−1}I)^s. The proof shows f(x) = x − H_λQ_λ(x+Z_λ) is a contraction of (z^{−1}I)^s whose fixed points are exactly the solutions.

items.name: Remark 2.2: the étale case
items.statement: If Λ′_1 is étale over Λ_1 there is H ∈ M_s(Λ_1{Z}) with the entries of HJ − 1 in (Q_1,…,Q_s); so if Q_λ(Z_λ) has coordinates in an ideal I and Λ_2 is separated and complete for the I-adic topology, one may take z = 1 and H_λ = H_λ(Z_λ) in Proposition 2.1, and Q_λ(Y) = 0 has a unique solution in Z_λ + I^s.
items.note: This is the form used throughout to extend operators from the framed ring R^+_{ϖ,□} to R^+_ϖ.

items.name: The arithmetic of K: ϖ, P_ϖ, i(K), K_n, δ_K
items.statement: F ⊂ K with K/F finite totally ramified of degree e; ϖ a uniformiser of K and P_ϖ its minimal polynomial over F, an Eisenstein polynomial of degree e. A compatible system (ζ_{p^n}) of p-power roots of unity with ζ_p ≠ 1; F_n = F(ζ_{p^n}), F_∞ = ∪F_n; i(K) is the largest n with ζ_{p^n} ∈ K; K_n = K(ζ_{p^{n+i(K)}}) so K_0 = K, K_∞ = ∪K_n; and δ_K := e·v_p(d_{K/F_{i(K)}}) ∈ N.
items.note: The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Enough roots of unity, precisely
items.statement: K contains enough roots of unity if v_p(d_{K/F_{i(K)}}) < 1/(2p) − 1/[F_{i(K)}:F], equivalently δ_K + [K:F_{i(K)}] < e/(2p). For fixed K, K(ζ_{p^n}) has enough roots of unity for all large n — a restatement of the fact that K_∞/F_∞ is almost étale — and it suffices to take n ≥ c(K)+2 (n ≥ c(K)+3 for p = 2), where c(K) is the conductor of K.
items.note: Quoted from Colmez's Astérisque paper for the sufficiency of n ≥ c(K)+2. This is the standing hypothesis of §§2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 3 and 4.

items.name: The framed algebra R_□ and the algebra R
items.statement: For integers h ∈ [1,e] (the multiplicity created by base change from a subfield) and a,b,c with d = a+b+c, R_□ := O_K{X,1/(X_1···X_a),ϖ^h/(X_{a+1}···X_{a+b})} = O_K{X,X_{d+1},X_{d+2}}/(X_{d+2}X_1···X_a − 1, X_{d+1}X_{a+1}···X_{a+b} − ϖ^h) with the spectral norm, and R is the p-adic completion of an étale algebra over R_□, so that R_□ is a system of coordinates (a frame) for R. The associated formal schemes carry the log structure induced by the divisor at infinity X_{a+b+1}···X_d = 0 and by the special fibre, and are log-smooth over O^×_K with semistable reduction.

items.name: The arithmetic base rings r^+_ϖ and r_ϖ
items.statement: r^+_ϖ := O_F[[X_0]] and r_ϖ := O_F[[X_0]]{X_0^{−1}}, with the log structure associated to X_0; X_0 ↦ ϖ gives a surjection r^+_ϖ → O_K.

items.name: The log-smooth lifts R^+_{ϖ,□} and R^+_ϖ
items.statement: With X′ = (X_0,X), R^+_{ϖ,□} is the completion of O_F[X′,1/(X_1···X_a),X_0^h/(X_{a+1}···X_{a+b})] for the (p,X_0)-adic topology, with X_0 added to the log structure; X_0 ↦ ϖ gives a surjection R^+_{ϖ,□} → R_□ with kernel generated by P = P_ϖ(X_0), so Spf R_□ ↪ Spf R^+_{ϖ,□} is a closed embedding into a formal log-scheme log-smooth over O_F. Writing R = R_□{Z}/(Q) with det(∂Q_i/∂Z_j) invertible and lifting the Q_j to R^+_{ϖ,□}, R^+_ϖ is the corresponding quotient of the (p,P)-adic completion of R^+_{ϖ,□}[Z]; it is étale over R^+_{ϖ,□} and log-smooth over O_F, and X_0 ↦ ϖ gives R^+_ϖ → R with kernel generated by P.

items.name: The PD envelope R^PD_ϖ
items.statement: R^PD_ϖ is the p-adic completion of R^+_ϖ[P^k/k!, k ∈ N]; since P ≡ X_0^e mod p, this equals R^+_ϖ[X_0^k/[k/e]!, k ∈ N]^∧, with the log structure induced from R^+_ϖ and X_0. Crystalline, hence syntomic, cohomology is defined by means of R^PD_ϖ.

items.name: The diagram (2.3) of formal log-schemes
items.statement: The commutative diagram containing the closed embeddings Spf R ↪ Spf R^+_ϖ, Spf R_□ ↪ Spf R^+_{ϖ,□} and Spf O_K ↪ Spf r^+_ϖ, the structure maps Spf R^+_ϖ → Spf R^+_{ϖ,□} → Spf r^+_ϖ → Spf O_F, and Spf R → Spf R^PD_ϖ → Spf R^+_ϖ.
items.note: Extended in §4.7 to the diagram defining the Fontaine–Messing period map.

items.name: The analytic rings on disks and annuli
items.statement: For 0 < u ≤ v: R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ is the p-adic completion of R^+_ϖ[p^{⌈vi/e⌉}/X_0^i, i ∈ N] and R^{(0,v]}_ϖ = R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ[1/X_0]; R^{[u]}_ϖ is that of R^+_ϖ[X_0^i/p^{[ui/e]}, i ∈ N]; R^{[u,v]}_ϖ is that of R^+_ϖ[X_0^i/p^{[ui/e]}, p^{⌈vi/e⌉}/X_0^i, i ∈ N]; and R_ϖ is that of R^+_ϖ[1/X_0]. Comparison with the PD envelope: R^{[u]}_ϖ ⊂ R^PD_ϖ if u ≤ 1/p, R^PD_ϖ ⊂ R^{[u]}_ϖ if u ≥ 1/(p−1), and for 1/p < u < 1/(p−1) there is C(u) with p^{C(u)}R^{[u]}_ϖ ⊂ R^PD_ϖ. The standing constraints on the radii are (p−1)/p ≤ u ≤ v/p < 1 < v < p·v_R and (1 + (p+1)/(2p(p−1)))u > 1/(p−1), satisfied by u = (p−1)/p, v = p−1 for p ≥ 3 and u = 3/4, v = 3/2 for p = 2.
items.note: These are the analytic coefficient rings the atlas builds at P7:annulus-foundations, here over a relative log base. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Remark 2.4: Laurent descriptions and reduction to the arithmetic variable
items.statement: Writing r^deco_ϖ for R^deco_ϖ with R = O_K: r^PD_ϖ = {Σ_{i∈N}a_iX_0^i/[i/e]!}, r^{[u]}_ϖ = {Σ_{i∈N}a_iX_0^i/p^{[iu/e]}} with a_i ∈ O_F → 0, the ring of analytic functions over F with integral values on the disk v_p(X_0) ≥ u/e; r^{[u,v]}_ϖ = {Σ_{i∈Z}a_iX_0^i} with v_p(a_i) ≥ −iv/e for i ≤ 0 and ≥ −iu/e for i ≥ 0, the functions with integral values on the annulus u/e ≤ v_p(X_0) ≤ v/e, so r^{[u]}_ϖ ⊂ r^{[u,v]}_ϖ with quotient involving only negative powers of X_0; r^{(0,v]+}_ϖ the functions with integral values on 0 < v_p(X_0) ≤ v/e; r_ϖ = {Σ_{i∈Z}a_iX_0^i} with a_i ∈ O_F → 0 as i → −∞. All the constructions touch only the arithmetic variable: R^deco_ϖ = r^deco_ϖ ⊗̂_{r^+_ϖ} R^+_ϖ for deco ∈ {PD, [u], (0,v]+, [u,v], ∅}, the completion being p-adic.

items.name: Remark 2.5: ℓ^0-presentations and extension by continuity
items.statement: With ℓ^0(X,Λ) the null sequences indexed by X = N or Z: (x_n) ↦ Σ x_nX_0^{−n} surjects ℓ^0(N,R^+_ϖ) → R_ϖ; (x_n) ↦ Σ x_np^{⌈nv/e⌉}X_0^{−n} surjects onto R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ; and the two-sided version surjects ℓ^0(Z,R^+_ϖ) → R^{[u,v]}_ϖ; the same holds with R^+_ϖ replaced by R^+_ϖ[[p/X_0^N]] when N ≥ 1 and u ≤ v < e/N. Consequently a continuous λ : R^+_ϖ → R^+_ϖ[[p/X_0^N]] with λ(X_0)/X_0^A a unit (A ≥ 1) extends by continuity to R_ϖ → R_ϖ, R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ → R^{(0,v/A]+}_ϖ and R^{[u,v]}_ϖ → R^{[u/A,v/A]}_ϖ for u ≤ v < e/N.
items.note: The mechanism by which ϕ_cycl, ι_cycl and the Γ_R-action are extended from R^+_ϖ to all the analytic rings.

items.name: The filtration by order of vanishing at X_0 = ϖ
items.statement: Each of the rings S above is filtered by the order of vanishing at X_0 = ϖ: if P is invertible in S[1/p] — which happens for S = R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ or R^{(0,v]}_ϖ with v < 1, for S = R^{[u,v]}_ϖ with 1 ∉ [u,v], and for S = R_ϖ — the filtration is trivial; otherwise one completes S[1/p] P-adically to get S ↪ R[1/p][[P]] = R[1/p][[X_0−ϖ]] and pulls back the filtration by powers of P.
items.note: The standing radii have 1 ∈ [u,v] but 1 ∉ [u,v/p], so R^{[u,v]}_ϖ is filtered and R^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ is not — which is why the complexes of §3 have an unfiltered target.

items.name: Remark 2.6: splitting off the filtration
items.statement: Any f ∈ r^PD_ϖ (resp. r^{[u]}_ϖ) is uniquely f^+ + f^− with f^+ ∈ F^r and f^− of degree ≤ re−1, hence f^− ∈ (1/(r−1)!)O_F[X_0] (resp. (1/p^{[ru]})O_F[X_0]); so any f ∈ R^PD_ϖ is f_1 + f_2 with f_1 ∈ F^rR^PD_ϖ and f_2 ∈ (1/(r−1)!)R^+_ϖ, and similarly in R^{[u]}_ϖ with f_2 ∈ (1/p^{[ru]})R^+_ϖ.

items.name: Admissible Frobenius
items.statement: A Frobenius on R_ϖ is a ring homomorphism lifting x ↦ x^p modulo p, hence restricting to the absolute Frobenius of O_F. It is admissible if ϕ(r_ϖ) ⊂ r_ϖ and there is v_0 > 1 with ϕ(R^{(0,v_0]+}_ϖ) ⊂ R^{(0,v_0/p]+}_ϖ and v^{(0,v_0/p]}(ϕ(X_j)/X_j^p − 1) > inf(1/(p−1),1/2) for 0 ≤ j ≤ d — the inequality that makes ϕ(x) − x^p admit divided powers (higher divided powers if p = 2). An admissible ϕ then satisfies ϕ(R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ) ⊂ R^{(0,v/p]+}_ϖ for all v ≤ v_0 and extends by continuity to R^{[u,v]}_ϖ for 0 < u ≤ v ≤ v_0.
items.note: The paper uses exactly two admissible Frobenii, ϕ_Kum and ϕ_cycl; they differ only on the arithmetic variable. ϕ_Kum computes crystalline and syntomic cohomology; ϕ_cycl is the Frobenius of (ϕ,Γ)-module theory and so is tied to étale cohomology. The authors note that Breuil–Kisin modules or Caruso ϕ,τ-modules might allow one to use ϕ_Kum throughout instead.

items.name: The Kummer Frobenius ϕ_Kum and the derivations ∂_{Kum,j}
items.statement: ϕ_Kum is defined on R^+_{ϖ,□} by ϕ_Kum(X_i) = X_i^p for 0 ≤ i ≤ d; by étaleness (Remark 2.2) it extends uniquely to R^+_ϖ, and by continuity to endomorphisms of S, S^PD, S^{[u]} and to S^{[u,v]} → S^{[u,v/p]}. The derivations ∂_{Kum,j} := X_j∂/∂X_j (0 ≤ j ≤ d) are defined on R^+_{ϖ,□}, hence on R^+_ϖ by étaleness, and extend to all R^deco_ϖ; they commute pairwise. For α ∈ {0,…,p−1}^{[0,d]}, u_{Kum,α} := X_0^{α_0}···X_d^{α_d} satisfies ∂_{Kum,j}u_{Kum,α} = α_ju_{Kum,α} and ϕ_Kum(u_{Kum,α}) = u_{Kum,α}^p.
items.note: The paper prints the last identity once with ϕ_cycl in place of ϕ_Kum, before ϕ_cycl has been defined; the correct form is restated nine lines later (source issue E3).

items.name: Lemma 2.7: a p-basis of R_ϖ/p
items.statement: (i) Every x ∈ R_ϖ/p is uniquely Σ_α c_{Kum,α}(x) with ∂_{Kum,j}c_{Kum,α}(x) = α_jc_{Kum,α}(x) for all j. (ii) There is a unique x_α ∈ R_ϖ/p with c_{Kum,α}(x) = x_α^p u_{Kum,α}. (iii) If x ∈ R^+_ϖ/p then c_{Kum,α}(x) ∈ R^+_ϖ/p and x_α ∈ X_0^{−h−1}R^+_ϖ/p, with x_α ∈ R^+_ϖ/p whenever α_i = 0 for i ≠ 0; in particular x_0 ∈ R^+_ϖ/p. The proof diagonalises the ∂_j (the operator ∂_j(∂_j−1)···(∂_j−(p−1)) vanishes on R_{ϖ,□}/p hence on R_ϖ/p by étaleness) and uses Tyc's theorem that X_0,…,X_d is a p-basis.
items.note: Tyc's p-basis theorem is quoted. The exponent −h−1 is where the semistable multiplicity h enters the constants.

items.name: Corollary 2.8: the decomposition over ϕ_Kum(R_ϖ)
items.statement: (i) Every x ∈ R_ϖ is uniquely Σ_α ϕ_Kum(x_α)u_{Kum,α} with x_α ∈ R_ϖ. (ii) If x ∈ R^+_ϖ then x_0 ∈ R^+_ϖ, all c_{Kum,α}(x) = ϕ_Kum(x_α)u_{Kum,α} lie in R^+_ϖ, and ∂_{Kum,j}c_{Kum,α}(x) − α_jc_{Kum,α}(x) ∈ pR^+_ϖ.

items.name: The operator ψ_Kum and the eigen-decomposition S = ⊕_α S_α
items.statement: ψ_Kum(x) := ϕ_Kum^{−1}(c_{Kum,0}(x)); intrinsically, R^+_ϖ[X_0^{−1}] is an extension of degree p^{d+1} of its ϕ_Kum-image with basis the u_{Kum,α}, so ψ_Kum = p^{−(d+1)}ϕ_Kum^{−1}∘Tr_{S/ϕ_Kum(S)}. It is not a ring morphism; it is a left inverse of ϕ_Kum with ψ_Kum(ϕ_Kum(x)y) = xψ_Kum(y), and ∂_{Kum,i}∘ϕ_Kum = pϕ_Kum∘∂_{Kum,i}, ∂_{Kum,i}∘ψ_Kum = p^{−1}ψ_Kum∘∂_{Kum,i}. It extends by continuity to R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ, R^{(0,v]}_ϖ and to surjections R^{[u]}_ϖ → R^{[pu]}_ϖ, R^{[u,v]}_ϖ → R^{[pu,pv]}_ϖ, and the maps c_{Kum,α} give decompositions S = ⊕_α S_α with S^{ψ_Kum=0} = ⊕_{α≠0}S_α.

items.name: Lemma 2.9: the derivations act by α_j modulo p
items.statement: For S = R^deco_ϖ with deco ∈ {∅,+,[u],(0,v]+,[u,v]}, ∂_{Kum,j} = α_j on S_α/pS_α.
items.note: This is what makes the ψ = 0 part of the Kummer complexes acyclic modulo p in §3.3.

items.name: The cyclotomic data: e_0, f, ζ, Q(X_0,T) and the variable T
items.statement: With K containing enough roots of unity: i = i(K), e_0 = [F_i:F] = (p−1)p^{i(K)−1}, f = [K:F_i] = e/e_0 and ζ = ζ_{p^i}. Since ζ−1 is a uniformiser of F_i one can choose A_0,…,A_{f−1} ∈ O_F[T] with v_T(A_j) ≥ 1 and v_T(A_0) = 1 such that Q(X_0,T) = X_0^f + A_{f−1}(T) X_0^{f−1} + ⋯ + A_0 has Q(X_0,ζ−1) as the minimal polynomial of ϖ over F_i. Let T ∈ r^+_ϖ be the solution of Q(X_0,T) = 0; then T = −α^{−1}X_0^f + ⋯ so X_0^{−f}T is a unit, r^+_ϖ = O_F[[T,X_0]]/Q(X_0,T) = ⊕_{j=0}^{f−1}O_F[[T]]X_0^j, and r_ϖ is étale over O_F[[T]]{T^{−1}}.

items.name: Lemma 2.10: the discriminant estimate
items.statement: With Q′ = ∂Q/∂X_0: (i) there are U ∈ O_F[X_0], a unit in O_F[[X_0]], and V,W ∈ O_F[X_0,T] with Q′(X_0,T) = X_0^{δ_K}U + pV + Q(X_0,T)W; (ii) the image Δ of Q′ in r^+_ϖ is invertible in r_ϖ and X_0^{−δ_K}Δ is a unit in O_F[[X_0,p/X_0^{δ_K}]]. The proof computes δ_K = e·v_p(Q′(ϖ,ζ−1)) = inf_{(k,p)=1}(f·v_T(A_k) + k−1) = v_{X_0}(Q̄′).
items.note: Quantifies the failure of r^+_ϖ/O_F[[T]] to be étale; it is the source of the constant δ_R.

items.name: The cyclotomic filtration generator P_0 and the element t
items.statement: Since X_0 ↦ ϖ sends T to ζ−1, the subring O_F[[T]] of r^+_ϖ is r^+_{ζ−1}, the filtrations may equivalently be defined by the order of vanishing at T = ζ−1, and one may use P_0 = ((1+T)^{p^i}−1)/((1+T)^{p^{i−1}}−1) in place of P. Set t := p^i log(1+T).
items.note: Under ι_cycl, P_0 maps to ξ and t to the usual t = log[ε] of p-adic Hodge theory.

items.name: Lemma 2.11: t generates the filtration up to a bounded power of p
items.statement: If (p−1)/p ≤ u ≤ v/p < 1 < v and 1/p < u then (i) t ∈ p·r^{[u,v]}_ϖ ∩ p·r^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ and (ii) multiplication by t^r is a p^{3r}-isomorphism r^{[u,v]}_ϖ ≅ F^rr^{[u,v]}_ϖ and a p^{2r}-isomorphism r^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ ≅ r^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ. The proof estimates inf_{s∈[u/e_0,v/e_0]}inf_{k≥1}(i + ks − v_p(k)) for the series of t, and shows that P_0^{−1}t is a unit of r^{[u,v]}_ϖ[1/p] and t a unit of r^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ[1/p] with the corrected denominators (E26).
items.note: The printed p^r and later filtered p^(2r) bounds fail; E26 gives a coarser arithmetic p^(3r) bound. Recompute downstream numerical losses. Coordinate repairs are in E32.

items.name: The cyclotomic frame R^+_{ζ−1,□} and the monoid M
The constant δ_R
items.statement: δ_R := ⌈δ_K/f⌉, so fδ_R − δ_K ≥ 0 and, because K has enough roots of unity, δ_R + 1 ≤ e_0/(2p) = (1/2)(p−1)p^{i−2}.
items.note: Every error term in §§2.3, 2.5, 2.6 is expressed through δ_R.

items.name: Proposition 2.12: extending a morphism from the cyclotomic frame to R^+_ϖ
items.statement: Let λ : R^+_{ζ−1,□} → Λ be continuous with λ(T)^{2δ_R} dividing p and Λ separated and complete for the (p/λ(T)^{2δ_R})-adic topology; let β : M → Λ be a morphism of monoids with β(X_i) = u_iλ(X_i) for 1 ≤ i ≤ d and β(X_0)^f = λ(T)u for units u_i, u; and let µ ∈ r^+_{ζ−1} be such that λ(µ)/λ(T)^{2δ_R} ∈ Λ is topologically nilpotent. If λ(µ) divides Q(β(X_0),λ(T)) and there is an ideal J ∋ λ(µ)/λ(T)^{1+δ_R} with Λ separated and complete J-adically such that λ extends to λ_ϖ : R^+_ϖ → Λ/J agreeing with β on M, then λ has a unique extension to R^+_ϖ lifting λ_ϖ with λ(X_0) ∈ β(X_0) + (λ(µ)/λ(T)^{δ_R})Λ. The proof applies Proposition 2.1 with z = λ(T)^{δ_R} and H_λ = Q′(β(X_0),λ(T))^{−1}, whose invertibility comes from Lemma 2.10, then extends over the two extra coordinates and finally over the étale part by Remark 2.2.
items.note: Applied three times: to ϕ_cycl (Proposition 2.13), to ι_cycl (Proposition 2.31) and to the Γ_R-action (Proposition 2.32).

items.name: ϕ_cycl on the frame, and the rings R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ
items.statement: ϕ_cycl on R^+_{ζ−1,□} sends T to (1+T)^p − 1 and X_i to X_i^p (1 ≤ i ≤ d), so ϕ_cycl(x) − x^p ∈ pR^+_{ζ−1,□}. Set v_R := e_0/(2pδ_R) = e/(2pfδ_R) > 1, R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ := R^+_ϖ[[p/T^{2pδ_R}]] = R^+_ϖ[[p/X_0^{2pfδ_R}]] and R^{(0,pv_R)}_ϖ := R^+_ϖ[[p/T^{2δ_R}]].
items.note: These round-bracket rings are a different family from the R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ: formal power series in p/X_0^{2pfδ_R} rather than p-adic completions.

items.name: Proposition 2.13 and the admissibility of ϕ_cycl
items.statement: ϕ_cycl has a unique extension to R^+_ϖ with ϕ_cycl(X_0) − X_0^p ∈ (p/T^{pδ_R})R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ and ϕ_cycl(x) − x^p ∈ (p/T^{p(1+δ_R)})R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ for x ∈ R^+_ϖ — note the target is R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ, not R^+_ϖ. Since ϕ_cycl(X_0)/X_0^p is a unit there, Remark 2.5 extends ϕ_cycl to R_ϖ → R_ϖ, R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ → R^{(0,v/p]+}_ϖ and R^{[u,v]}_ϖ → R^{[u/p,v/p]}_ϖ for u ≤ v < v_R, and this Frobenius is admissible.

items.name: Lemma 2.14: ϕ_cycl-descent of the annulus
items.statement: If v < pv_R and x ∈ R_ϖ has ϕ_cycl(x) ∈ R^{(0,v/p]+}_ϖ then x ∈ R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ. The proof writes R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ = Σ_{n≥0}(p^n/X_0^{[ne/v]})R^+_ϖ and constructs the expansion of x term by term.

items.name: The operator ψ_cycl after the cyclotomic decomposition
items.statement: After Proposition 2.15, define ψ_cycl(x)=ϕ_cycl^(−1)(c_(cycl,0)(x))=p^(−d−1)ϕ_cycl^(−1)Tr_(R_ϖ/ϕ_cycl(R_ϖ))(x). Prove integrality from the monomial decomposition, ψ_cyclϕ_cycl=1, ψ_cycl(ϕ_cycl(a)b)=aψ_cycl(b), and ∂_jψ_cycl=p^(−1)ψ_cycl∂_j on the stated domains. It is an additive semilinear projection, not a ring homomorphism.

items.name: Proposition 2.15: the cyclotomic decomposition of R_ϖ
items.statement: (i) Every x ∈ R_ϖ is uniquely Σ_α c_{cycl,α}(x) with c_{cycl,α}(x) ∈ ϕ_cycl(R_ϖ)u_{cycl,α}. (ii) If v < v_R and x ∈ R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ then c_{cycl,α}(x) ∈ X_0^{−pδ_K}R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ for all α. The proof is §2.3.6: first the analogous decomposition in the Kummer monomials (Lemma 2.21), then the change of basis of Lemma 2.22.
items.note: The paper writes the object of (ii) as x_{cycl,α}, a symbol it never defines; the two later uses fix it as c_{cycl,α}(x) (source issue E33).

items.name: Proposition 2.16: ψ_cycl on the disk rings
items.statement: If v < pv_R: (i) ψ_cycl(T^{−pN}R^{(0,v/p]+}_ϖ) ⊂ T^{−N−δ_R}R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ; (ii) with ℓ_R := ⌈(p/(p−1))δ_R⌉, the ring T^{−ℓ_R}R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ is ψ_cycl-stable; (iii) if moreover v ≤ p, the natural map ⊕_{α≠0}ϕ_cycl(R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ)u_{cycl,α} → (R^{(0,v/p]+}_ϖ)^{ψ_cycl=0} is a p^{p+1}-isomorphism. The proof of (iii) uses Proposition 2.15(ii), Lemma 2.14 and the divisibility of X_0^{h+1+δ_K} by p^{p+1}, which needs h ≤ e, δ_K+1 ≤ e/p and v ≤ p.
items.note: The p^{p+1} of (iii) and the constant ℓ_R are exactly what appear in §4.5 (Lemma 4.10 and the definition of the ψ-Koszul complexes).

items.name: Lemma 2.17: the estimate for ∂_{cycl,0}X_0
items.statement: If v < 2pv_R then ∂_{cycl,0}X_0 ∈ X_0^{−δ_K}r^{(0,v]+}_ϖ and v^{(0,v]}(∂_0X_0) ≥ −1. It follows from Q(X_0,T) = 0 by implicit differentiation, ∂_0X_0 = −(1+T)(∂Q/∂X_0)^{−1}(∂Q/∂T), together with Lemma 2.10.

items.name: The polycircle localisations R^deco_{ϖ,i}
items.statement: Let I := {a+1,…,a+b,d+1}, so ∏_{i∈I}X_i = X_0^h. For i ∈ I, R^+_{ϖ,□,i} and R^+_{ϖ,i} are obtained by localising where X_j is a unit for j ∈ I∖{i}, that is S_i = S{Y}/(1 − Y∏_{j∈I∖{i}}X_j). Then R^+_{ϖ,i} is étale over R^+_{ϖ,□,i}, which is smooth (not merely log-smooth) over O_F, since the relation becomes X_i = YX_0^h and removes X_i from the variables; the rings R^deco_{ϖ,i} are then built as before, and ϕ extends to them.
items.note: Smoothness of the local pieces is what makes the p-basis argument of Lemma 2.20 available.

items.name: Lemma 2.18: membership in R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ is local on the polycircles
items.statement: For x ∈ R_ϖ: x ∈ R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ if and only if x ∈ R^{(0,v_R)}_{ϖ,i} for all i ∈ I. The proof shows first that divisibility by X_0 in each R^+_{ϖ,i}/p implies divisibility in R^+_ϖ/p — geometrically, that ∪_iZ_i is Zariski dense in Z = Spec(R^+_ϖ/(p,X_0)), which holds for the frame and then by étaleness — and then constructs the expansion x = Σ s(a_n)p^n/X_0^{nM} with M = 2pfδ_R.
items.note: The paper prints the rings here as R^{(0,r_R)}, with a symbol r_R that is defined nowhere; v_R is meant (source issue E4).

items.name: Lemma 2.19: lifting a p-basis decomposition to characteristic 0
items.statement: Let S = r_ϖ or R_{ϖ,i} and (u_j)_{j∈J} a family in S^+ such that every x ∈ S/p is uniquely Σ_j c_j(x)^pu_j with c_j(x) ∈ S, and such that for some N ≤ 2fδ_R, x ∈ S^+/p implies c_j(x) ∈ X_0^{−N}S^+/p. Then every x ∈ S is uniquely Σ_j ϕ(c_j(x))u_j with c_j(x) ∈ S, and x ∈ S^{(0,v_R)} implies c_j(x) ∈ X_0^{−N}S^{(0,pv_R)}. The proof is an explicit successive-approximation algorithm built from a section s of reduction satisfying s(X_0y) = X_0s(y).

items.name: The local index sets A_i and monomials u_{i,β}
Lemma 2.20: the local decomposition
items.statement: For i ∈ I: (i) every x ∈ R_{ϖ,i} is uniquely Σ_{β∈A_i}x_{i,β} with x_{i,β} ∈ ϕ(R_{ϖ,i})u_{i,β}; (ii) if x ∈ R^{(0,v_R)}_{ϖ,i} then all x_{i,β} ∈ R^{(0,v_R)}_{ϖ,i}. The proof notes that the X_j with j ≠ i form a basis of the differentials of R^+_{ϖ,□,i}/p, hence by Tyc's theorem the u_{i,β} form a basis over the Frobenius image, and applies Lemma 2.19 with N = 0.

items.name: Lemma 2.21: the Kummer decomposition with integral bounds
items.statement: (i) For x ∈ R_ϖ the components x_α of the decomposition lie in ϕ(R_ϖ)u_{Kum,α}. (ii) If v < v_R and x ∈ R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ then x_α ∈ R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ for all α. The proof reduces by Remark 2.5 to R^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ, then by Lemma 2.18 to the polycircles, then by Lemma 2.20 to exhibiting x_α as a combination of the x_{i,β} with coefficients in r^{(0,v_R)}_ϖ, which is done by an explicit expansion of X_0^N in the ϕ-basis.

items.name: Lemma 2.22: the Kummer-to-cyclotomic change of basis
items.statement: For k ≥ 0 there are a_{k,i} ∈ T^{−δ_R}r^{(0,pv_R)}_ϖ with X_0^k = Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}ϕ(a_{k,i})(1+T)^i. The proof uses the trace from r_ϖ to r_{ζ−1}, the dual basis g_j = Δ^{−1}R_j of (X_0^j) for the trace form — so g_j ∈ X_0^{−δ_K}r^+_ϖ/p by Lemma 2.10 — and Lemma 2.19 with S = r_ϖ and N = fδ_R. Consequently u_{Kum,α} = Σ_i ϕ(a_{α_0,i})u_{cycl,β_i} with β_i = (i,α_1,…,α_d), so c_{cycl,α}(x) = Σ_i ϕ(a_{i,α_0})x_{(i,α_1,…,α_d)}, which together with Lemma 2.21 proves Proposition 2.15.
items.note: The factor T^{−δ_R} here is the source of the δ_R in Proposition 2.16(i).

items.name: The big extension R̄ and its Galois group
items.statement: R̄ is the maximal extension of R unramified outside X_{a+b+1}···X_d = 0 in characteristic 0, that is after inverting p, and G_R := Gal(R̄/R); v_p denotes the spectral valuation on R̄[1/p].
items.note: G_R is the group whose continuous cohomology the main local theorem computes.

items.name: Tilts, Witt vectors and the period rings A_S, E_S
items.statement: For S = K̄ or R̄[1/p], C(S) is the completion of S for v_p — a perfectoid algebra — and C^+(S) its subring of elements of valuation ≥ 0. E_S is the tilt of C(S), describable as the set of sequences (x_n) in C(S) with x_{n+1}^p = x_n, and A_S := W(E_S); for x ∈ C(S), x^♭ denotes any element of E_S with x_0 = x. v_E(x) := v_p(x^♯) with x^♯ := x_0 is the spectral valuation function for which E_S is complete (do not assume multiplicativity for an arbitrary relative affinoid); E^+_S is its subring of elements of valuation ≥ 0, the tilt of C^+(S), equal to lim(C^+(S)/a, x ↦ x^p) for a = {v_p ≥ 1/p}, and A^+_S := W(E^+_S). Every element of A_S is uniquely Σ_k p^k[x_k] with x_k ∈ E_S. The inclusions K̄ ⊂ R̄[1/p] and O_K̄ ⊂ R̄ induce E_K̄ ⊂ E_R̄, A_K̄ ⊂ A_R̄, E^+_K̄ ⊂ E^+_R̄ and A^+_K̄ ⊂ A^+_R̄.
items.note: The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: ε, π, ξ, θ, B^+_dR and A_cr
items.statement: ε := (1,ζ_p,ζ_{p^2},…) ∈ E^+_K̄, π := [ε] − 1 ∈ A^+_K̄ and ξ := π/ϕ^{−1}(π). θ : A^+_S → C^+(S), Σ p^k[x_k] ↦ Σ p^kx_k^♯, is a surjective ring homomorphism whose kernel is principal, generated by p − [p^♭], by P_ϖ([ϖ^♭]) or by ξ; extended Q_p-linearly, B^+_dR(S) is the completion of A^+_S[1/p] for the ideal (p−[p^♭]), filtered by its powers. A_cr(S) is the p-adic completion of A^+_S[(p−[p^♭])^k/k!, k ∈ N] = A^+_S[[p^♭]^k/k!, k ∈ N], naturally a subring of B^+_dR(S). Also π_i := ϕ^{−i}(π).
items.note: The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: The period rings on disks and annuli
items.statement: For v > 0 and S = K̄, R̄: A^{(0,v]}_S := {Σ p^k[x_k] : v·v_E(x_k) + k → +∞} and A^{(0,v]+}_S its subring where v·v_E(x_k) + k ≥ 0 for all k, so A^{(0,v]}_S = A^{(0,v]+}_S[1/[p^♭]]; equivalently, for α ∈ E^+_K̄ with v_E(α) = 1/v, A^{(0,v]+}_S is the p-adic completion of A^+_S[p/[α]]. For β with v_E(β) = 1/u, A^{[u]}_S is the p-adic completion of A^+_S[[β]/p], and A^{[u,v]}_S that of A^+_S[p/[α],[β]/p]. When the radii bracket 1 these rings embed into B^+_dR(S) and inherit its filtration. Frobenius acts by ϕ(A^{(0,v]+}_S) = A^{(0,v/p]+}_S, ϕ(A^{[u]}_S) = A^{[u/p]}_S and ϕ(A^{[u,v]}_S) = A^{[u/p,v/p]}_S.
items.note: The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Comparison of A_cr with the annulus rings
items.statement: A_cr(R̄) ⊂ A^+_R̄[[β]/p]^∧ for 0 < v_E(β) ≤ p−1 and A_cr(R̄) ⊃ A^+_R̄[[β]/p]^∧ for v_E(β) ≥ p, with a constant p^{C(v)} in between; hence A_cr(R̄) ⊂ A^{[u]}_R̄ for u ≥ 1/(p−1) and A_cr(R̄) ⊃ A^{[u]}_R̄ for u ≤ 1/p. In particular for p > 2 and u = (p−1)/p one has A_cr(R̄) ⊂ A^{[u]}_R̄, while for p = 2 and u = 1/2 one has A_cr(R̄) ⊃ A^{[1/2]}_R̄ and also A_cr(R̄) ⊂ ϕ^{−1}(A^{[1/2]}_R̄). The proof compares [p^♭]^{[k]} = [p^♭]^kp^{−(k−s_k)/(p−1)}u_0 with powers of [β]/p using v_p(k!) = (k−s_k)/(p−1).
items.note: The period-ring analogue of the R^{[u]}_ϖ versus R^PD_ϖ comparison; it is what lets the crystalline and the (ϕ,Γ)-complexes be compared.

items.name: The fundamental exact sequence and the twist t{r}
items.statement: For r ∈ N there is the fundamental exact sequence 0 → Z_p·t{r} → F^rA_cr --p^r−ϕ--> A_cr with t{r} := t^{b(r)}(t^{p−1}/p)^{a(r)} for r = (p−1)a(r) + b(r), 0 ≤ b(r) ≤ p−1; moreover p^r−ϕ is p^r-surjective. Z_p(r)′ := (1/p^{a(r)})Z_p(r).
items.note: Recalled without proof; generalised by Lemma 2.23. The displayed kernel normalization is not a closed implementation contract until the ambiguity E31 is resolved. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Lemma 2.23: Artin–Schreier and fundamental sequences
items.statement: (i) For v > 0 there are exact sequences 0 → Z_p → A_R̄ --1−ϕ--> A_R̄ → 0 (2.24) and 0 → Z_p → A^{(0,v]+}_R̄ --1−ϕ--> A^{(0,v/p]+}_R̄ → 0. (ii) 0 → Z_p(r)′ → F^rA_cr(R̄) --p^r−ϕ--> A_cr(R̄) → 0 is p^r-exact. (iii) For 0 < u ≤ 1 ≤ v the sequence 0 → Z_p(r) → F^rA^{[u,v]}_R̄ --p^r−ϕ--> A^{[u,v/p]}_R̄ → 0 is p^{4r}-exact. All the surjections have continuous sections. The proof of (iii) splits into the two sequences 0 → Z_p(r) → (A^{[u,v]}_R̄)^{ϕ=p^r} → A^{[u,v]}_R̄/F^r → 0 and 0 → (A^{[u,v]}_R̄)^{ϕ=p^r} → A^{[u,v]}_R̄ --p^r−ϕ--> A^{[u,v/p]}_R̄ → 0, compares them with the crystalline versions through the p^r-isomorphisms A_cr(R̄)^{ϕ=p^r} ≅ (A^{[u]}_R̄)^{ϕ=p^r} ≅ (A^{[u,v]}_R̄)^{ϕ=p^r}, and treats p = 2 separately.
items.note: Parts (i) and (ii) are quoted from Andreatta–Iovita and Tsuji; (iii) is proved here.

items.name: Remark 2.30: surjectivity of P(ϕ) on B^+_cr ⊗ M
items.statement: For M a ϕ-module over F (a finite rank F-vector space with semilinear Frobenius isomorphism) and P ∈ F[X] with P(0) ≠ 0, the map P(ϕ) : B^+_cr ⊗_F M → B^+_cr ⊗_F M is surjective, where B^+_cr = A_cr[1/p]. The proof reduces by Dieudonné–Manin to a standard slope module, then to a single polynomial R with all roots of one valuation, and shows that the inverse series converges on [p^♭]B^+_cr while R(ϕ^h) is surjective on A^+_K̄[1/p] because E_K̄ is algebraically closed with ring of integers A^+_K̄/p.
items.note: Dieudonné–Manin is invoked, not proved.

items.name: The Kummer embedding ι_Kum
items.statement: Choosing compatible p-power roots X_i^{p^{−n}} inside R̄ and setting X_i^♭ = (X_i,X_i^{1/p},…) ∈ E^+_R̄, the assignment X_0 ↦ [ϖ^♭], X_i ↦ [X_i^♭] defines an embedding ι_Kum : R^+_{ϖ,□} → A_R̄ commuting with Frobenius and compatible with filtrations; by étaleness it extends to R^+_ϖ → A_R̄ and by continuity to R^PD_ϖ → A_cr(R̄), R^{[u]}_ϖ → A^{[u]}_R̄ and R^{[u,v]}_ϖ → A^{[u,v]}_R̄, commuting with ϕ_Kum and the filtrations.

items.name: The tower R_n, R_∞ and the group Γ_R
items.statement: R^cycl_□ := O_{F_i}{X_1,…,X_d} and R^cycl_{□,n} := O_{F_{i+n}}{X_1^{p^{−n}},…,X_d^{p^{−n}}}; R_n is the integral closure of R in the subalgebra of R̄[1/p] generated by R and R^cycl_{□,n}, and R_∞ = ∪_n R_n. Then R_∞[1/p] is Galois over R[1/p] with group Γ_R sitting in 1 → Γ′_R → Γ_R → Γ_K → 1, where Γ′_R = Gal(R_∞[1/p]/K_∞R[1/p]) ≅ Z_p^d, Γ_K = Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ 1 + p^{i(K)}Z_p, and a ∈ 1 + p^{i(K)}Z_p acts on Z_p^d by multiplication by a.
items.note: Γ_R is the group whose continuous cohomology computes the étale cohomology in §4; the semidirect product is the arithmetic-times-geometric structure the Koszul complexes are built on.

items.name: Proposition 2.31 and the element π_K: the cyclotomic embedding
items.statement: ι_cycl : R^+_{ζ−1,□} → A^+_{R̄} sends T to π_i = ϕ^{−i}(π) and X_j to [X_j^♭]; it commutes with Frobenius (ϕ∘ι_cycl = ι_cycl∘ϕ_cycl) and with filtrations, since P_0 ↦ P_0(π_i) = ξ. It has a unique extension to R^+_ϖ → A^+_R̄[[p/π_i^{2δ_R}]] with ι_cycl(X_0) − [ϖ^♭] ∈ (ξ/π_i^{δ_R})A^+_R̄[[p/π_i^{2δ_R}]] and θ∘ι_cycl the projection R^+_ϖ → R (Proposition 2.31, by Proposition 2.12 with µ = P_0 and J = ker θ). Setting π_K := ι_cycl(X_0) one has θ(π_K) = ϖ and, for n ∈ N, ϖ_n := θ(ϕ^{−n}(π_K)) is a uniformiser of K_n; since π_K/[ϖ^♭] is a unit, Remark 2.5 extends ι_cycl to embeddings R_ϖ ↪ A_R̄, R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ ↪ A^{(0,v]+}_R̄ and R^{[u,v]}_ϖ ↪ A^{[u,v]}_R̄ for u ≤ v < pv_R, commuting with Frobenius and filtration.
items.note: The paper prints ϖ_n = θ(ϕ^{−1}(π_K)), whose right-hand side does not depend on n (source issue E5).

items.name: The image rings A^deco_R
items.statement: A^deco_R (resp. A^deco_{R,□}) denotes the image of R^deco_ϖ (resp. R^deco_{ζ−1,□}) under ι_cycl; A^+_{R,□} is stable under G_R, which acts through Γ_R.
items.note: Note the clash of notation the paper carries: A^deco_R without a bar is this small image ring, while A^deco_R̄ is the big period ring of §2.4.2. The identification R^{[u,v]}_ϖ ≅ A^{[u,v]}_R is what transports a Γ_R-action onto the syntomic complexes.

items.name: The generators γ_0,…,γ_d of Γ_R and their action
items.statement: With c := exp(p^i), so that a := p^{−i}(c−1) ∈ Z_p^*, one can choose topological generators γ_j of Γ_R with γ_0(π_i) = (1+π_i)^c − 1 = (1+π)^a(1+π_i) − 1 and γ_j(π_i) = π_i for 1 ≤ j ≤ d; γ_k([X_k^♭]) = [ε][X_k^♭] = (1+π)[X_k^♭] and γ_j([X_k^♭]) = [X_k^♭] for j ≠ k. Then γ_1,…,γ_d topologically generate Γ′_R, and on R^+_{ζ−1,□} the action reads γ_0(T) = (1+T)^{p^ia}(1+T) − 1, γ_j(X_j) = (1+T)^{p^i}X_j, with γ_k(T) = T for k ≠ 0 and γ_k(X_j) = X_j for k ≠ j.

items.name: Proposition 2.32 and Corollary 2.33: the Γ_R-action on the analytic rings
items.statement: Any continuous γ : R^+_{ζ−1,□} → R^+_{ζ−1,□} of the shape γ(X_j) = (1+T)^{p^ia_j}X_j, γ(T) = (1+T)^{p^ia_0}(1+T) − 1 extends uniquely to R^+_ϖ → R^+_ϖ[[p/T^{2δ_R}]] with γ(x) − x ∈ (((1+T)^{p^i}−1)/T^{1+δ_R})R^+_ϖ[[p/T^{2δ_R}]] and γ(X_0) − X_0 in the same ideal with exponent δ_R (Proposition 2.32, again by Proposition 2.12). Consequently (Corollary 2.33): (i) the Γ_R-action extends uniquely to R_ϖ, stabilises R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ for v < pv_R and extends continuously to R^{[u,v]}_ϖ for u ≤ v < pv_R, and is trivial modulo T^{−1−δ_R}((1+T)^{p^i}−1); (ii) A_R, A^{(0,v]+}_R, A^{(0,v]}_R and A^{[u,v]}_R are G_R-stable with G_R acting through Γ_R, and ι_cycl is Γ_R-equivariant.

items.name: The infinitesimal action: log γ_j = t∂_j
items.statement: The action of Γ_R on A^{[u,v]}_R[1/p] is analytic and its Lie algebra acts by log γ_j = t∂_j for 0 ≤ j ≤ d, where ∂_j is transported from ∂_{cycl,j}.
items.note: This identity is the bridge between the differential operators of the syntomic side and the group cohomology of the (ϕ,Γ) side; it is what §4.1 and §4.4 exploit.

items.name: Lemma 2.34: the (γ−1)-filtration estimates
items.statement: For u ≤ v < p and S = R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ or R^{[u,v]}_ϖ: (γ−1)·T^n(p,T^{e_0})^kS ⊂ T^{n+p^{i−1}−δ_R−1}(p,T^{e_0})^{k+1}S, and (γ−1)^k·S ⊂ T^{k(p^{i−1}−δ_R−1)}(p,T^{e_0})^kS. The proof combines the triviality of γ modulo T^{−1−δ_R}((1+T)^{p^i}−1), the twisted-derivation rule for γ−1, the divisibility of (1+T)^{p^{i−1}}−1 by T^{p^{i−1}} (valid since v < p), and the membership ((1+T)^{p^i}−1)/((1+T)^{p^{i−1}}−1) ∈ (p,T^{e_0}) from Lemma 2.35.
items.note: The paper prints the first exponent as n+p^{i−1}−δ_R, which is inconsistent both with its own proof and with the second display, the k-fold iterate (source issue E6). The estimate is what makes ∇_j/τ_j invertible in Lemma 4.6, and the roots-of-unity hypothesis enters exactly here.

items.name: Lemma 2.35: divisibility estimates for π, π_1 and π_i
items.statement: For v < p: π_i^{−p^{i−1}}π_1 is a unit of A^{(0,v]+}_R̄; p is divisible by π_i^{[(p−1)p^{i−1}/v]}, hence by π_i^{(p−1)p^{i−2}}; p^2/π_1 ∈ A^{(0,v]+}_R̄ and is divisible by π_i^{(2(p−1)−v)p^{i−2}}; and π/π_1 ∈ (p,π_i^{(p−1)p^{i−1}})A^{(0,v]+}_R̄ is divisible by π_i^{(p−1)p^{i−2}}, hence by π_i^{δ_R+1}. The proof works in r^{(0,v]+}_{ζ−1}, where π_i becomes T and π_1 becomes (1+T)^{p^{i−1}}−1, on the annulus 0 < v_p(T) ≤ v/((p−1)p^{i−1}), and uses the identity π/π_1 = π_1^{p−1} + pπ_1^{p−2} + ⋯ + p.
items.note: Note π/π_1 = ξ. The paper prints the identity as π = π_1^{p−1} + pπ_1^{p−2} + ⋯ + p, which has a constant term and so cannot be π (source issue E7).

items.name: The fat rings SΛ⟨s⟩ and their filtration
items.statement: For S = R^PD_ϖ or R^{[u,v]}_ϖ, Λ a p-adically complete filtered O_F-algebra and ι : S → Λ a continuous injective filtered morphism, let f : S ⊗ Λ → Λ be x⊗y ↦ ι(x)y, and let SΛ⟨s⟩ be the p-adically completed log-PD envelope of level s of f — that is, the p-adic completion of S ⊗ Λ with the elements (x⊗1 − 1⊗ι(x))^{[k]} for x ∈ S and (V_j−1)^{[k]} for V_j := (X_j⊗1)/(1⊗ι(X_j)), 0 ≤ j ≤ d, adjoined, where x^{[k]} = x^k/[k/p^s]!. Adding the (V_j−1)^{[k]} is exactly what makes it logarithmic. f extends to SΛ⟨s⟩ → Λ, and F^rSΛ⟨s⟩ is the closure of the ideal generated by products x_1x_2∏(V_j−1)^{[k_j]} with x_1 ∈ F^{r_1}S, x_2 ∈ F^{r_2}Λ and r_1 + r_2 + Σk_j ≥ r.
items.note: The paper writes the filtration condition with x_1 ∈ F^{r_1}R_1 and x_2 ∈ F^{r_2}R_2, symbols that are only introduced in §3.6 (source issue E8).

items.name: Lemma 2.36: the structure theorem for the fat rings
items.statement: (i) Every x ∈ SΛ⟨s⟩ is uniquely Σ_{k∈N^{d+1}}x_k∏_{j=0}^d(1−V_j)^{[k_j]} with x_k ∈ Λ tending to 0. (ii) x ∈ F^rSΛ⟨s⟩ if and only if x_k ∈ F^{r−|k|}Λ for all k. The proof identifies SΛ⟨s⟩ with Λ[(1−V_j)^{[k]}]^∧: injectivity by applying f after the operators ∂_j, surjectivity by constructing ι_0 : S_□ → Λ′ explicitly on monomials and extending it by étaleness.
items.note: The workhorse of §2.6: Lemmas 2.37, 2.38 and 2.40 all reduce to it.

items.name: Lemma 2.37: the filtered Poincaré lemma
items.statement: With Ω^1 = ⊕_{j=0}^d Z·dX_j/X_j and Ω^n = ∧^nΩ^1, so Ω^n_{SΛ⟨s⟩/Λ} = SΛ⟨s⟩ ⊗ Ω^n filtered by F^rΩ^•, the natural map F^rΛ → F^rΩ^•_{SΛ⟨s⟩/Λ} is a p^s-quasi-isomorphism. The contracting homotopy is written out explicitly on the basis of Lemma 2.36, the correcting factor (k_j!/(k_j+δ)!)([(k_j+δ)/p^s]!/[k_j/p^s]!) having valuation between −s and 0 — which is why the result is only a p^s-quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: With s = 0 for p ≥ 3 and s = 1 for p = 2 this is the 2-exactness used in Lemma 3.11 and in the comparison diagram of §4.7.

items.name: The fat period rings E^PD_R̄, E^{[u,v]}_R, E^{[u,v]}_{R_∞}, E^{[u,v]}_R̄
items.statement: Take s = 0 if p ≥ 3 and s = 1 if p = 2. Then E^{[u,v]}_R and E^{[u,v]}_{R_∞} are SΛ⟨s⟩ for S = R^{[u,v]}_ϖ, Λ = A^{[u,v]}_R or A^{[u,v]}_{R_∞} and ι = ι_cycl; E^PD_R̄ is SΛ⟨s⟩ for S = R^PD_ϖ, Λ = A_cr(R̄) and ι = ι_Kum; and E^{[u,v]}_R̄ is SΛ⟨s⟩ for S = R^{[u,v]}_ϖ, Λ = A^{[u,v]}_R̄ and ι = ι_Kum.
items.note: E^PD_R̄ is the ring through which the Fontaine–Messing period map is defined in §4.7.

items.name: Lemma 2.38 and Remark 2.39: inclusions, and ι_cycl for E^{[u,v]}_R̄
items.statement: (i) E^PD_R̄ ⊂ E^{[u,v]}_R̄; (ii) E^{[u,v]}_R ⊂ E^{[u,v]}_{R_∞} ⊂ E^{[u,v]}_R̄. The essential point in (ii) is that (π_K−[ϖ^♭])/[ϖ^♭] admits divided powers of level s in A^{[u,v]}_R̄, which follows from (π_K−[ϖ^♭])/[ϖ^♭] ∈ (ξ/π_i^{δ_R+1})A^+_R̄[[p/π_i^{2δ_R}]] together with ξ = π_i^{e_0} + pα and the valuation estimate v^{[u,v]}((π_K−[ϖ^♭])/[ϖ^♭]) ≥ 1/((p−1)p^s), using 2p(δ_R+1) ≤ e_0, u ≥ (p−1)/p and v < p. It follows from the proof (Remark 2.39) that E^{[u,v]}_R̄ could equally be defined with ι_cycl in place of ι_Kum.
items.note: Remark 2.39 is what makes the change of Frobenius in Proposition 3.10 possible: the same fat ring receives both the Kummer and the cyclotomic complex.

items.name: Lemma 2.40: Frobenius and Galois action on the fat period rings
items.statement: (i) ϕ extends uniquely to continuous morphisms E^PD_R̄ → E^PD_R̄, E^{[u,v]}_R → E^{[u,v/p]}_R, E^{[u,v]}_{R_∞} → E^{[u,v/p]}_{R_∞} and E^{[u,v]}_R̄ → E^{[u,v/p]}_R̄. (ii) The G_R-action extends uniquely and continuously to all four rings, commuting with ϕ, and E^{[u,v]}_{R_∞} is the fixed subring of E^{[u,v]}_R̄ under Gal(R̄[1/p]/R_∞[1/p]). The proof reduces by Lemma 2.36 to checking divided powers of (1−ϕ(V_j)) and (1−σ(V_j)): for ι_Kum this is immediate since ϕ(V_j) = V_j^p, and for ι_cycl one uses the admissibility of ϕ_cycl and, for the arithmetic variable, that (π_K−σ(π_K))/σ(π_K) ∈ π_i^{−δ_R−1}πA^{[u,v]}_R̄ is divisible by ξ (Lemma 2.35), which has divided powers.

items.name: Example 2.41: the fat ring in dimension 0 is Â_st
items.statement: For R = O_K one has E^PD_R̄ = Â_st, the p-adic completion of A_cr[Y^k/k!, k ∈ N] with Y = X_0/[ϖ^♭] − 1; then ϕ(Y) = (1+Y)^p − 1 and σ(Y) = [ε]^{−c(σ)}(1+Y) − 1 for σ ∈ G_K with σ([ϖ^♭]) = [ε]^{c(σ)}[ϖ^♭]. Conceptually Â_{st,n} = H^0_cr(O^×_{K,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}) and Â_st = lim_n of these.
items.note: Identifies the construction in dimension 0 with Fontaine's semistable period ring Â_st, which is the object CDN20's extraction meets again as Â_st ≅ RΓ_cr(O^×_{C,n}/r^PD_{ϖ,n}).

items.name: The chain Syn(R,r) ≃ Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) and its four steps
items.statement: Assume K contains enough roots of unity. §3 produces comparisons up to controlled p-power torsion, after truncation at r where specified, between the complex computing syntomic cohomology and a complex closer to Galois cohomology, as the composite Syn(R,r) := Kum(R^PD_ϖ,r) ≃ Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) ≃ Kum_ψ(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) ≃ Kum_ψ(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) ≃ Kum(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) ≃ Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r), realised by Proposition 3.3(i), Lemma 3.4, Lemma 3.6, the diagram in the proof of Corollary 3.9, and Proposition 3.10. The last step — the change of Frobenius from ϕ_Kum to ϕ_cycl — is the main one, and it forces the detour through R^{[u,v]}_ϖ because ϕ_cycl is not defined on R^PD_ϖ (except when K = F is absolutely unramified). In dimension 0, with ∂_Kum = X_0 d/dX_0 and ∂_cycl = (1+T) d/dT, the two end complexes are Syn(O_K,r) : F^r r^PD_ϖ --(∂_Kum, p^r−ϕ_Kum)--> F^{r−1}r^PD_ϖ ⊕ r^PD_ϖ --(−(p^r−pϕ_Kum)+∂_Kum)--> r^PD_ϖ and Cycl(r^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) : F^r r^{[u,v]}_ϖ --(∂_cycl, p^r−ϕ_cycl)--> F^{r−1}r^{[u,v]}_ϖ ⊕ r^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ --(−(p^r−pϕ_cycl)+∂_cycl)--> r^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ. The standing choice of radii is u = (p−1)/p, v = p−1 for p ≥ 3 and u = 3/4, v = 3/2 for p = 2.

items.name: The triples (S,S′,S″) and the divided Frobenius on forms
items.statement: For S = R^PD_ϖ, R^{[u]}_ϖ, R^{[u,v]}_ϖ set S′ = R^PD_ϖ, R^{[u]}_ϖ, R^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ respectively, so that ϕ_Kum(S) ⊂ S′ in all three cases; and for S = R^{[u]}_ϖ, R^{[u,v]}_ϖ set S″ = R^{[pu]}_ϖ, R^{[pu,v]}_ϖ, so that ψ_Kum(S) ⊂ S″. With J_i = {0 ≤ j_1 < ⋯ < j_i ≤ d} and ω_j = dX_{j_1}/X_{j_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dX_{j_i}/X_{j_i}, both ϕ_Kum and ψ_Kum act on Ω^i_S coefficientwise in this basis: ϕ_Kum(Σ_j f_j ω_j) = Σ_j ϕ_Kum(f_j) ω_j and likewise for ψ_Kum. This is not the natural Frobenius — with it d(ϕ(f)) = pϕ(df) — and the natural one is p^i·ϕ_Kum on Ω^i; the division by powers of p is forced by the need for an integral left inverse ψ, and is why the factors p^• appear in the complexes below. F^rΩ^i_S is the sub-S-module generated by F^rS·Ω^i_S, so F^rΩ^i_S = ⊕_{j∈J_i} F^rS·ω_j, and the de Rham complex is filtered by F^rΩ^•_S := F^rS → F^{r−1}Ω^1_S → F^{r−2}Ω^2_S → ⋯

items.name: The Kummer complex Kum(S,r) and the syntomic complex Syn(R,r)
items.statement: Kum(S,r) := [F^rΩ^•_S --(p^r − p^•ϕ_Kum)--> Ω^•_{S′}], the mapping fibre whose degree-i component is p^r − p^iϕ_Kum : F^{r−i}Ω^i_S → Ω^i_{S′}. The syntomic complex and syntomic cohomology of R are Syn(R,r) := Kum(R^PD_ϖ,r) and H^*_syn(R,r) := H^*(Syn(R,r)); mod p^n, Syn(R,r)_n := Syn(R,r) ⊗_Z Z/p^n and H^*_syn(R_n,r) := H^*(Syn(R,r)_n). Explicitly Syn(R,r) = Cone(F^rΩ^•_{R^PD_ϖ} --(p^r − p^•ϕ_Kum)--> Ω^•_{R^PD_ϖ})[−1] with Ω^•_{R^PD_ϖ} := R^PD_ϖ ⊗_{R^+_ϖ} Ω^•_{R^+_ϖ/O_F}.

items.name: The ψ-variant Kum_ψ(S,r) and the cyclotomic complex Cycl(S,r)
items.statement: Kum_ψ(S,r) := [F^rΩ^•_S --(p^rψ_Kum − p^•)--> Ω^•_{S″}] for S = R^{[u]}_ϖ, R^{[u,v]}_ϖ, with degree-i component p^rψ_Kum − p^i : F^{r−i}Ω^i_S → Ω^i_{S″}. For S = R^{[u,v]}_ϖ only, Cycl(S,r) := [F^rΩ^•_S --(p^r − p^•ϕ_cycl)--> Ω^•_{S′}]; it cannot be defined for S = R^PD_ϖ or R^{[u]}_ϖ because ϕ_cycl does not carry those rings into the corresponding S′ unless K = F.

items.name: The X_0-valuation and the subrings S_N
items.statement: For S = r^PD_ϖ or r^{[u]}_ϖ, v_{X_0} : S → N ∪ {+∞} is the valuation relative to X_0: for f = Σ a_i X_0^i, v_{X_0}(f) = inf{i ∈ N : a_i ≠ 0}; and for N ∈ N, S_N := {f ∈ S : v_{X_0}(f) ≥ N}. R^PD_{ϖ,N} and R^{[u]}_{ϖ,N} are the topological closures of r^PD_{ϖ,N} ⊗_{r^+_ϖ} R^+_ϖ and r^{[u]}_{ϖ,N} ⊗_{r^+_ϖ} R^+_ϖ in R^PD_ϖ and R^{[u]}_ϖ.
items.note: The paper prints this definition with the second tensor factor as R^{[u]}_{ϖ,N} and the ambient rings as R^PD_{ϖ,N} and R^{[u]}_{ϖ,N}, which is circular; the corrected reading is recorded here (source issue E12).

items.name: Lemma 3.1: bijectivity of 1 − p^{−s}ϕ on S_N
items.statement: Let S = R^PD_ϖ or R^{[u]}_ϖ. For s ∈ Z and N ≥ 1 the map (1 − p^{−s}ϕ) : S_N[1/p] → S_N[1/p] is bijective, with inverse Σ_{k∈N} p^{−ks}ϕ^k. Moreover: (a) for S = R^PD_ϖ there is a constant N(r,e) — for S = R^{[u]}_ϖ a constant N(r,e,u) — such that 1 − p^{−s}ϕ is p^{N(r,e)}-bijective on S_1 for all s ≤ r; (b) if N ≥ se (for S = R^PD_ϖ), resp. N ≥ se/(u(p−1)) (for S = R^{[u]}_ϖ), then 1 − p^{−s}ϕ is bijective on S_N. The convergence comes from inf_{i≥1}(v_p([p^k i/e]!) − v_p([i/e]!) − ks) = v_p([p^k/e]!) − ks ≥ p^{k−1}/e − 1 − ks → +∞, and the constant may be taken to be N(r,e) = ceil(max(0,sup_{k≥0}(1 + kr − p^{k−1}/e))).
items.note: The paper prints N(r,e) = inf_{k∈N}(−1−kr+p^{k−1}/e), which is negative, where a nonnegative exponent is needed; the sign is corrected here (source issue E9).

items.name: Lemma 3.2: p^s − ϕ on the change-of-disk quotients
items.statement: Let r,s ∈ N. (i) If 1/(p−1) ≤ u ≤ 1 then p^s − ϕ induces a p^{s+r}-isomorphism F^rΩ^i_{R^{[u]}_ϖ}/F^rΩ^i_{R^PD_ϖ} ≅ Ω^i_{R^{[u]}_ϖ}/Ω^i_{R^PD_ϖ}. (ii) If u′ ≤ u ≤ pu′ then p^s − ϕ induces a p^{s+r}-isomorphism F^rΩ^i_{R^{[u]}_ϖ}/F^rΩ^i_{R^{[u′]}_ϖ} ≅ Ω^i_{R^{[u]}_ϖ}/Ω^i_{R^{[u′]}_ϖ}. In the ω_j-basis the map in degree i is p^s − p^iϕ, so the case i = 0 suffices; p^s-injectivity uses F^rA = A ∩ F^rB together with ϕ(B) ⊂ A and p^s x = (p^s−p^iϕ)x + p^iϕ(x), and surjectivity up to p^{s+r} uses Lemma 3.1 and the splitting of Remark 2.6.

items.name: Proposition 3.3: change of disk of convergence
items.statement: (i) For 1/(p−1) ≤ u ≤ 1 the morphism of complexes Kum(R^PD_ϖ,r) → Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) induced by R^PD_ϖ ⊂ R^{[u]}_ϖ is a p^{6r}-quasi-isomorphism. (ii) If u′ ≤ u ≤ pu′ the morphism Kum(R^{[u′]}_ϖ,r) → Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) induced by R^{[u′]}_ϖ ⊂ R^{[u]}_ϖ is a p^{6r}-quasi-isomorphism. In particular Syn(R,r) = Kum(R^PD_ϖ,r) is computed by Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) up to p^{6r}.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) ≃ Kum_ψ(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r)
items.statement: The commutative square with rows (p^r − p^•ϕ) : F^rΩ^•_{R^{[u]}_ϖ} → Ω^•_{R^{[u]}_ϖ} and (p^rψ − p^•) : F^rΩ^•_{R^{[u]}_ϖ} → Ω^•_{R^{[pu]}_ϖ}, identity on the left and ψ on the right, defines a quasi-isomorphism Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) → Kum_ψ(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) — with no constant. The proof: ψ is surjective on Ω^•, so only the kernel complex 0 → S^{ψ=0} → (Ω^1_S)^{ψ=0} → ⋯ has to be shown acyclic; S^{ψ=0} = ⊕_{α≠0} S_α over α ∈ {0,…,p−1}^{d+1}, the de Rham complex splits accordingly, and modulo p Lemma 2.9 turns the α-part into the total complex of a (d+1)-cube with all vertices S_α and the arrow in direction i equal to α_i, which is acyclic because some α_i is invertible.

items.name: Lemma 3.5: the filtration is invisible on the annulus quotient
items.statement: If u ≤ 1 ≤ v the natural morphism F^rR^{[u,v]}_ϖ/F^rR^{[u]}_ϖ → R^{[u,v]}_ϖ/R^{[u]}_ϖ is a p^r-isomorphism; modulo p^n it is a p^r-injection. The proof reduces to R = O_K and writes p = X_0^e A + BP with A,B ∈ r^+_ϖ, hence p^{r+[kv]} = B_kP^r + A_kX_0^{e[kv]}, which exhibits p^{r+[kv]}X_0^{−ke} as a sum of an element of F^rr^{[u,v]}_ϖ and an element of r^{[u]}_ϖ.

items.name: Lemma 3.6: change of annulus of convergence
items.statement: Let u ≤ 1 ≤ v. The natural morphism Kum_ψ(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) → Kum_ψ(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) induces a p^{2r}-quasi-isomorphism τ^{≤r}Kum_ψ(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) ≅ τ^{≤r}Kum_ψ(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r), and the same modulo p^n. Equivalently the mapping fibre (3.7) = [F^rΩ^•_{R^{[u,v]}_ϖ}/F^rΩ^•_{R^{[u]}_ϖ} --(p^rψ−p^•)--> Ω^•_{R^{[pu,v]}_ϖ}/Ω^•_{R^{[pu]}_ϖ}] is p^{2r}-acyclic in degrees ≤ r: by Lemma 3.5 the filtration can be ignored, R^{[u,v]}_ϖ/R^{[u]}_ϖ ≅ R^{[pu,v]}_ϖ/R^{[pu]}_ϖ, and 1 − p^sψ with s = r−i ≥ 0 is invertible there with inverse 1 + p^sψ + p^{2s}ψ^2 + ⋯, convergent even for s = 0 because ψ is topologically nilpotent.

items.name: Remark 3.8: truncation is avoidable at a cost
items.statement: Truncating at degree r is not strictly necessary at this point, since ψ is very rapidly nilpotent, but the constants that then appear involve log e.
items.note: An assertion without proof; it explains why the statements of Lemma 3.6 and Corollary 3.9 are truncated.

items.name: Corollary 3.9: Kum on a disk versus on an annulus
items.statement: For pu ≤ v the natural map Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) → Kum(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) := [F^rΩ^•_{R^{[u,v]}_ϖ} --(p^r−p^•ϕ)--> Ω^•_{R^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ}] induces a p^{2r}-quasi-isomorphism τ^{≤r}Kum(R^{[u]}_ϖ,r) ≅ τ^{≤r}Kum(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r). The proof composes Lemma 3.4, Lemma 3.6 and one more square (identity on the left, ψ on the right) whose quasi-isomorphy follows by the argument of Lemma 3.4.
items.note: The paper prints the constant as p^{2c_e+2r}, and c_e is defined nowhere in it; the constant produced by the quoted proof is p^{2r}, since the two outer steps are quasi-isomorphisms with no constant (source issue E11).

items.name: The generic complex S(A,r,ϕ) of a filtered pair with Frobenius
items.statement: For filtered rings A ⊂ A′ with a Frobenius ϕ : A → A′, S(A,r,ϕ) := [F^rΩ^•_A --(p^r − p^•ϕ)--> Ω^•_{A′}], where ϕ on Ω^n_A is the Frobenius divided by p^n. Thus Kum(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) = S(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r,ϕ_Kum) and Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) = S(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r,ϕ_cycl).

items.name: Proposition 3.10: change of Frobenius
items.statement: The complexes Kum(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) and Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) are 2^{2(d+1)}-quasi-isomorphic. The proof uses the identification (A^{[u,v]}_R,ϕ) ≅ (R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,ϕ_cycl) and Lemma 2.40 to produce morphisms S(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r,ϕ_Kum) → S(Ē^{[u,v]}_R,r,ϕ) ← S(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r,ϕ_cycl) into the level-s log-PD envelope, each a 2^{d+1}-quasi-isomorphism by the filtered Poincaré lemma of Lemma 3.11. The base of the constant is 2, not p: it comes from the partial divided-power level s, which is 0 for p ≥ 3 and 1 for p = 2.
items.note: This is the step the section exists for — the passage from the crystalline Frobenius to the (ϕ,Γ)-module Frobenius — and the only one carried out by crystalline rather than (ϕ,Γ)-module techniques.

items.name: Two copies of R^{[u,v]}_ϖ and the PD envelope R_3
items.statement: Let R_1, R_2 be two copies of R^{[u,v]}_ϖ with isomorphisms ι_i : R^{[u,v]}_ϖ → R_i and X_{i,j} = ι_i(X_j) for i = 1,2 and 0 ≤ j ≤ d; let R_3 := (R_1 ⊗ R_2)^PD with respect to ι = ι_2∘ι_1^{−1}, so that R_3 ≅ Ē^{[u,v]}_R as a ring, without the actions of G_R or ϕ. With Ω^1_i = ⊕_{j=0}^{d} Z·dX_{i,j}/X_{i,j} for i = 1,2, Ω^1_3 := Ω^1_1 ⊕ Ω^1_2 and Ω^n_i := ∧^nΩ^1_i, one has Ω^n_{R_3} = R_3 ⊗ Ω^n_3, filtered as usual by F^rΩ^•_{R_3} := F^rR_3 → F^{r−1}R_3⊗Ω^1_3 → ⋯

items.name: Lemma 3.11: the filtered Poincaré lemma for two copies
items.statement: The natural maps F^rΩ^•_{R_1} → F^rΩ^•_{R_3} ← F^rΩ^•_{R_2} are 2^{d+1}-quasi-isomorphisms. The proof takes the ∂_{R_1}-filtered Poincaré lemma 0 → F^rR_2 → F^rR_3 --∂_{R_1}--> F^{r−1}R_3⊗Ω^1_1 --∂_{R_1}--> ⋯ , which is 2-exact by Lemma 2.37 with S = R_1 and Λ = R_2, extends it over the de Rham complex of R_2 using that the contracting homotopy of Lemma 2.37 is R_2-linear, and identifies the total complex of the resulting double complex with F^rΩ^•_{R_3}.

items.name: The complexes HK(S,r) and DR(S,r)
items.statement: For S = R^PD_ϖ, ϕ = ϕ_Kum and r ≥ 0: HK(S,r) := [Ω^•_S --(p^r − p^•ϕ)--> Ω^•_S] and DR(S,r) := Ω^•_S/F^r, so that the degree-i term of DR(S,r) is Ω^i_S/F^{r−i}Ω^i_S, zero for i ≥ r. One has τ^{≤r−1}DR(S,r) ≅ DR(S,r), the natural map τ^{≤r+1}HK(S,r) → HK(S,r) is a p^{2r}-quasi-isomorphism (because 1 − p^sϕ is invertible on Ω^{r+s}_S for s ≥ 1), and Syn(R,r) = [HK(S,r) → DR(S,r)].

items.name: Proposition 3.12: syntomic cohomology between Hyodo–Kato and de Rham
items.statement: (i) The natural map τ^{≤r+1}Syn(R,r) → Syn(R,r) is a p^{2r}-quasi-isomorphism, and H^{r+1}(Syn(R,r)) ≅ H^{r+1}(HK(S,r)). (ii) The complex τ^{≤r−1}HK(S,r) is p^N-acyclic for a constant N = N(e,d,p,r); hence DR(S,r) → τ^{≤r−1}Syn(R,r)[1] is a p^N-quasi-isomorphism. (iii) Both statements hold modulo p^n, and H^{r+1}(HK(S,r)_n) is, étale locally on R_n, p^{N(r)}-trivial. The proof of (ii) removes the X_0-part by Lemma 3.1, replaces S by S̄ = S/X_0S ≅ R^+_ϖ/X_0, uses Lemma 3.13 to get a left inverse ψ of ϕ on S̄ with ψ∂_i = p∂_iψ, and then inverts p^rψ − p^i in degrees i ≤ r−1; the last claim of (iii) reduces modulo p to the surjectivity of x ↦ x − x^p, which holds étale locally because Artin–Schreier extensions are étale.
items.note: This is the structural description of syntomic cohomology that §5 uses: up to universal torsion it is the cone of a Hyodo–Kato term over a de Rham term.

items.name: Lemma 3.13: ψ_Kum stabilises X_0R^+_ϖ
items.statement: ψ = ψ_Kum stabilises X_0R^+_ϖ. The proof computes ψ = p^{−d−1}ϕ^{−1}∘Tr with Tr = Tr_{R^+_ϖ/ϕ(R^+_ϖ)} as a sum over the conjugates σ_η(x) for η a tuple of p-th roots of unity acting by X_i ↦ η_iX_i, so that X_0 | x implies X_0 | Tr(x); then ϕ(x) ∈ X_0R^+_ϖ implies x ∈ X_0R^+_ϖ by successive approximation, and X_0R^+_ϖ[1/p] ∩ R^+_ϖ = X_0R^+_ϖ removes the denominator.

items.name: Lemma 3.14: DR(S,r) is the silly truncation of the de Rham complex
items.statement: After inverting p, DR(S,r) is quasi-isomorphic to σ^{≤r−1}Ω^•_R, where σ^{≤r−1} is the silly (non-derived) truncation. The proof uses r^+_ϖ[1/p]/F^r ≅ K[P]/P^r, hence S[1/p]/F^r ≅ R ⊗_{O_K}(K[P]/P^r), writes DR(S,r) as the total complex of a double complex whose rows are the de Rham complexes of R with coefficients K[P]/P^s, and kills the subcomplex on which ∂_0 : PK[P]/P^r ≅ K[P]/P^{r−1} is an isomorphism.

items.name: Remark 3.15: the top degree of DR is not de Rham cohomology
items.statement: By Lemma 3.14, H^i(DR(S,r)) = H^i_dR(Spf R) after inverting p for i ≤ r−2, but H^{r−1}(DR(S,r)) is much bigger than H^{r−1}_dR(Spf R), because differential forms are taken modulo exact rather than modulo closed forms: for r = 1, H^0(DR(S,r)) is all of R, not the constants.
items.note: Assertion without proof; it is the reason the comparison of Corollary 3.16 stops at i ≤ r−1.

items.name: The logarithmic de Rham complex of the generic fibre
items.statement: For X a semistable formal scheme over O_K (locally of the standard form with h = 1), X_{K,tr} := X^an_K ∖ D for D the divisor at infinity and X^an_K the associated rigid analytic space, and RΓ_dR(X_K, log D) := RΓ(X^an_K, Ω^•_{X^an_K}(log D)). For X quasi-compact, RΓ_dR(X_K, log D) ≅ RΓ(X,Ω^•_{X/O^×_K})_Q := (holim_n RΓ(X_n,Ω^•_{X_n/O^×_{K,n}}))_Q.

items.name: Corollary 3.16: de Rham cohomology maps to syntomic cohomology
items.statement: For X a quasi-compact formal semistable scheme over O_K, the natural map H^{i−1}_dR(X_(K,tr))→H^i_syn(X,r)_Q is an isomorphism for 1≤i≤r−1 and injective for i=r. Use Lemma 3.17 only unfiltered. Compose its inverse with log de Rham→log de Rham/F^r; since F^r is supported in degrees ≥r this is an isomorphism on H^j for j≤r−2 and an injection for j=r−1. Lemma 3.14 identifies the quotient with DR locally, and Proposition 3.12(ii) then gives the stated ranges. Do not use a filtered quasi-isomorphism to the open de Rham complex.

items.name: Lemma 3.17: log de Rham cohomology computes the open one
items.statement: For a semistable formal scheme X over O_K the natural morphism RΓ_dR(X_K, log D) → RΓ_dR(X_{K,tr}) is an unfiltered quasi-isomorphism; the stronger filtered assertion is false for the usual Hodge filtration (E28). The proof compares both with the complex Ω^•_{X^an_K}(∗D) of meromorphic differentials along D: the map Ω^•_{X^an_K}(∗D) → j_*Ω^•_{X_{K,tr}} is a quasi-isomorphism by Kiehl [38, Theorem 2.3] (and Rj_* = j_* because j is quasi-Stein), while r : Ω^•_{X^an_K}(log D) → Ω^•_{X^an_K}(∗D) admits a residue map with Res∘r = id and a homotopy between r∘Res and the identity, following Kiehl's computations.
items.note: The one place in §3 where the key step is quoted: Kiehl's de Rham comparison for meromorphic differentials on rigid spaces. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Remark 3.18: the syntomic exponential is not surjective
items.statement: The explicit computation of the syntomic cohomology of R = O^×_K shows that α_{r,r} need not be surjective: for r = 1 an extra Z_p appears in H^1_syn(O^×_K,r). In higher dimensions the discrepancy is far larger, by Remark 3.15.

items.name: The subring O^{(r)}_K
items.statement: O^{(r)}_K := O_K ∩ (R^PD_ϖ + P^rF[X_0]_P), the intersection being taken inside the P-adic completion K[[P]] = K[[X_0 − ϖ]] through the embedding of §2.2.5. One has O^{(1)}_K = O_K.

items.name: Proposition 3.19: the syntomic cohomology of O^×_K
items.statement: (i) For r ≥ 2: H^0_syn(O^×_K,r) is p^{13r}-isomorphic to 0; H^1_syn(O^×_K,r) is p^{N(r,e)}-isomorphic to O^{(r)}_K; H^2_syn(O^×_K,r) is p^{N(r,e)}-isomorphic to 0. (ii) For r = 1 there are p^{N(r,e)}-isomorphisms H^0_syn(O^×_K,r) ≅ 0, H^1_syn(O^×_K,r) ≅ O^{(r)}_K ⊕ Z_p and H^2_syn(O^×_K,r) ≅ O_F/(ϕ−1).
items.note: Stated by the authors without proof ("We will state the following proposition without a proof") and not attributed to another paper; a design job must plan it as an obligation, not import it. It is what Remark 3.18 rests on.

items.name: Standing setup of §4 and the dimension-0 model
items.statement: K contains enough roots of unity; u = (p−1)/p and v = p−1 for p ≥ 3, u = 3/4 and v = 3/2 for p = 2; i = i(K) is the largest integer with ζ_{p^i} ∈ K, e_0 = [F_i:F] = (p−1)p^{i(K)−1}, δ_R = ⌈δ_K/f⌉ with f = [K:F_i], and the roots-of-unity hypothesis implies δ_R + 1 ≤ e_0/(2p), which gives the convergence inequality (1 + (p^{i−1}−δ_R−1)/e_0)u ≥ (1 + 1/(p−1) − 1/(2p))u > 1/(p−1) for all p. The isomorphism R^{[u,v]}_ϖ ≅ A^{[u,v]}_R of filtered rings with Frobenius transports a Γ_R-action onto the complexes of §3, which is what relates Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) to the complexes of (ϕ,Γ)-module theory. In dimension 0 the comparison to be proved is between Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rA^{[u,v]}_K) : F^rA^{[u,v]}_K --(∂,p^r−ϕ)--> F^{r−1}A^{[u,v]}_K ⊕ A^{[u,v/p]}_K --−(p^r−pϕ)+∂--> A^{[u,v/p]}_K and Herr's complex Kos(ϕ,Γ_K,A_K(r)) : A_K(r) --(τ_0,1−ϕ)--> A_K(r)^2 --−(1−ϕ)+τ_0--> A_K(r), where τ_0 = γ_0 − 1 for γ_0 the chosen topological generator of Γ_K. The two steps are: kill the filtration by dividing by powers of t, which turns ∂ into the action of Lie Γ_R (Lemma 4.4); and pass from Lie Γ_R to Γ_R by analyticity (Proposition 4.5). The rest is (ϕ,Γ)-module technique for changing the domain of convergence.

items.name: From differential forms to Koszul complexes
items.statement: With ω_0 = dT/(1+T), ω_j = dX_j/X_j for 1 ≤ j ≤ d and ω_j = ω_{j_1}∧⋯∧ω_{j_i} for j ∈ J_i, the ω_j form a basis of F^aΩ^i_S over F^aS, so the de Rham differential becomes the family of operators ∂_j. Define Kos(∂,F^rS) := F^rS --(∂_j)--> (F^{r−1}S)^{J_1} → (F^{r−2}S)^{J_2} → ⋯ and Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rR^{[u,v]}_ϖ) := [Kos(∂,F^rR^{[u,v]}_ϖ) --p^r−p^•ϕ_cycl--> Kos(∂,R^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ)], so that Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rR^{[u,v]}_ϖ) ≅ Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r). Separating the arithmetic variable X_0 from the geometric ones: J′_i ⊂ J_i is the set of multi-indices with j_1 ≠ 0, ∂′ = (∂_1,…,∂_d), Kos(∂′,F^rS) is the corresponding subcomplex, and Kos(∂,F^rS) = [Kos(∂′,F^rS) --∂_0--> Kos(∂′,F^{r−1}S)]. Transporting along ι_cycl gives the tautological identification Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rR^{[u,v]}_ϖ) ≅ Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rA^{[u,v]}_R), written as a 2×2 homotopy limit with horizontal maps p^r−p^•ϕ and p^r−p^{•+1}ϕ and vertical maps ∂_0. The gain is an action of Γ_R whose infinitesimal action is related to the differentials by ∇_j := log γ_j = t∂_j for 0 ≤ j ≤ d.
items.note: Footnote 9 records that ∂_0 should strictly be multiplied by p to be defined, and that this is ignored throughout because it changes nothing in the arguments.

items.name: Koszul resolutions over the Iwasawa algebra
items.statement: For S = Z_p[[τ_1,…,τ_d]], K(τ_1,…,τ_d) := K(τ_1) ⊗̂ ⋯ ⊗̂ K(τ_d) with K(τ_i) = (0 → Z_p[[τ_i]] --τ_i--> Z_p[[τ_i]] → 0); its degree-q term is ∧^q_S S^d and the differential is d^1_q(a_{i_1⋯i_q}) = Σ_{k=1}^q (−1)^{k+1} a_{i_1⋯î_k⋯i_q} τ_{i_k} (4.1). With Z_p[[Γ′_R]] := lim_H Z_p[Γ′_R/H] ≅ Z_p[[τ_1,…,τ_d]] for τ_j := γ_j − 1, this is a resolution of Z_p by topological Z_p[[Γ′_R]]-modules; the same with τ^c_j := γ^c_j − 1 for c = exp(p^i) gives K(τ^c_1,…,τ^c_d). For Λ := Z_p[[Γ_R]], K(Λ) is the corresponding complex of Λ-modules, and by Morita's lemma [44, Lemma 4.3] lim_m (Z_p[Γ_K/(Γ_K)^{p^m}] ⊗_{Z_p} K(τ_1,…,τ_d)) ≅ K(Λ), so K(Λ) resolves Z_p[[Γ_K]]. The map τ_0 : K^c(Λ) → K(Λ) is γ_0 − 1 in degree 0 and (a_{i_1⋯i_q}) ↦ (a_{i_1⋯i_q}(γ_0 − δ_{i_1⋯i_q})) in degree q, where δ_{i_1⋯i_q} = δ_{i_q}⋯δ_{i_1} and δ_{i_j} = (γ^c_{i_j}−1)(γ_{i_j}−1)^{−1}, a unit in Z_p[[Γ′_R]] because γ_j − 1 is topologically nilpotent; it is a map of complexes by the identity (γ_0 − δ_{i_1⋯i_q}) = τ^c_{i_q}⋯τ^c_{i_1}τ^0_0τ^{−1}_{i_1}⋯τ^{−1}_{i_q}. Finally K(Λ,τ) := [K^c(Λ) --τ_0--> K(Λ)] resolves Z_p in topological left Λ-modules, using the exact sequence 0 → Z_p[[Γ_K]] --γ_0−1--> Z_p[[Γ_K]] → Z_p → 0.
items.note: The paper prints that last exact sequence without its Z_p term (source issue E14). Morita [44, Lemma 4.3] is quoted.

items.name: Group Koszul complexes and Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,S(r))
items.statement: For a topological Γ_R-module M, Kos(Γ′_R,M) := Hom_{Λ,cont}(K(Λ),M) = M --(τ_j)--> M^{J′_1} → ⋯ → M^{J′_d}, and Kos^c(Γ′_R,M) is the same with τ^c_j; τ_0 induces a map of complexes Kos(Γ′_R,M) → Kos^c(Γ′_R,M), and Kos(Γ_R,M) := Hom_{Λ,cont}(K(Λ,τ),M) = [Kos(Γ′_R,M) --τ_0--> Kos^c(Γ′_R,M)]. For S = A^{[u,v]}_R, A^{(0,v]+}_R, A_R with S′ = A^{[u,v/p]}_R, A^{(0,v/p]+}_R, A_R, and S(r) the module S with the Γ_R-action twisted by χ^r, Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,S(r)) is the 2×2 homotopy limit with rows 1−ϕ : Kos(Γ′_R,S(r)) → Kos(Γ′_R,S′(r)) and 1−ϕ : Kos^c(Γ′_R,S(r)) → Kos^c(Γ′_R,S′(r)) and vertical maps τ_0.

items.name: The Lazard–Mahler comparison λ : Kos(Γ_R,M) ≃ RΓ_cont(Γ_R,M)
items.statement: Let X_• be Lazard's standard complex computing RΓ_cont(Λ,M) := Hom_{Λ,cont}(X_•,M) and Y_• the standard complex of Γ_R with RΓ_cont(Γ_R,M) computed by continuous cochains Hom_{Z_p[Γ_R],cont}(Y_•,M). Lazard [42, V.1.2.6], through Mahler's theorem, shows that the map induced by Y_• → X_• factors through the continuous cochains and gives RΓ_cont(Λ,M) ≅ RΓ_cont(Γ_R,M); comparing the two projective resolutions K(Λ,τ) and X_• of Z_p (possible and unique up to homotopy by [42, V.1.1.5.1]) gives a functorial quasi-isomorphism Kos(Γ_R,M) ≅ RΓ_cont(Λ,M), unique in the derived category. Composing, λ : Kos(Γ_R,M) ≅ RΓ_cont(Γ_R,M).
items.note: Lazard's results and Mahler's theorem are quoted, not proved.

items.name: The Lie-algebra Koszul complexes
items.statement: Kos(Lie Γ′_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) is the complex A^{[u,v]}_R(r) → A^{[u,v]}_R(r)^{J′_1} → ⋯ → A^{[u,v]}_R(r)^{J′_d} with the differentials of (4.1) and τ_j replaced by ∇_j; the map ∇_0 between two copies of it is ∇_0 − qp^i in degree q, and Kos(ϕ,Lie Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) is the 2×2 homotopy limit with rows 1−ϕ and vertical maps ∇_0.
items.note: Degree q uses ∇_0−q p^i; see the commuting-square check in E29.

items.name: Proposition 4.2: group Koszul versus filtered differential Koszul
items.statement: There exist a universal constant N and a natural p^{Nr}-quasi-isomorphism τ^{≤r}Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) ≅ τ^{≤r}Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rA^{[u,v]}_R). ('Natural' means defined by universal formulas.) It is the composite of Proposition 4.5 (an honest quasi-isomorphism) and Lemma 4.4 with its numerical loss recomputed from E26 (the source prints p^{40r}).

items.name: Remark 4.3: the Lie algebras and the t^r-twist
items.statement: Lie Γ′_R = Z_p[∇_j, 1 ≤ j ≤ d] is free of rank d and commutative; Lie Γ_R = Z_p[∇_j, 0 ≤ j ≤ d] is free of rank d+1 with [∇_j,∇_l] = 0 for 1 ≤ j,l ≤ d and [∇_0,∇_j] = p^i∇_j for 1 ≤ j ≤ d. The Koszul complexes above compute Lie-algebra cohomology: RΓ(Lie Γ′_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) ≅ Kos(Lie Γ′_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) and RΓ(Lie Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) ≅ [Kos(Lie Γ′_R,·) --∇_0--> Kos(Lie Γ′_R,·)], whence Kos(ϕ,Lie Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) ≅ [RΓ(Lie Γ_R,·) --1−ϕ--> RΓ(Lie Γ_R,·)]. Moreover, by Lemma 2.11, multiplication by t^r gives a p^{3r} filtration comparison F^rA^{[u,v]}_R ≅ t^rA^{[u,v]}_R after transporting the arithmetic estimate, and a separate p^{2r} comparison t^rA^{[u,v/p]}_R ≅ A^{[u,v/p]}_R, and becomes Galois-equivariant after twisting the source by χ^r.

items.name: Lemma 4.4: killing the filtration by powers of t
items.statement: There is a natural comparison τ^{≤r}Kos(ϕ,Lie Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r))→τ^{≤r}Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rA^{[u,v]}_R), with a universal p-power loss linear in r, and a finite-coefficient version. Its construction uses multiplication by powers of t degree by degree and the Frobenius/arithmetic-direction comparison square. Truncation at r is essential. Source Lemma 4.4 specifies 40r and 80r; those explicit constants are left as an unclosed numerical obligation after correcting the filtration bound E26, not asserted as independently verified replacements.
items.note: The source states 40r and 80r. Recompute these numerical exponents from the corrected filtration loss E26; this review does not certify the printed constants. The existence of some universal linear loss is not refuted.

items.name: Proposition 4.5: the integral Lazard comparison
