items.statement: There is a natural quasi-isomorphism Laz : Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) ≅ Kos(ϕ,Lie Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) — with no constant. It is (β,β^c) of Lemma 4.6 and Remark 4.7.
items.note: The paper refers to this statement as "Lemma 4.5" in the §4 preamble and in the proof of Theorem 4.14 (source issue E15).

items.name: The comparison maps β and β^c
items.statement: For M = A^{[u,v]}_R(r) or A^{[u,v/p]}_R(r): β : Kos(Γ′_R,M) → Kos(Lie Γ′_R,M) is the identity in degree 0 and β_q(a_{i_1⋯i_q}) = (∇_{i_q}⋯∇_{i_1}τ^{−1}_{i_1}⋯τ^{−1}_{i_q}(a_{i_1⋯i_q})) for 1 ≤ q ≤ d; β^c : Kos^c(Γ′_R,M) → Kos(Lie Γ′_R,M) is β^c_0 = ∇_0τ^{−1}_0 and β^c_q(a_{i_1⋯i_q}) = (∇_{i_q}⋯∇_{i_1}∇_0τ^{−1}_0τ^{c,−1}_{i_1}⋯τ^{c,−1}_{i_q}(a_{i_1⋯i_q})). Here τ_j = γ_j − 1 for 1 ≤ j ≤ d, τ^c_j = γ^c_j − 1, and on S(r) one has τ_0 = c^rγ_0 − 1 = (c^r−1)γ_0 + (γ_0−1), the factor c^r coming from the twist.

items.name: Lemma 4.6: β and β^c are well-defined isomorphisms
items.statement: The maps β and β^c are well-defined isomorphisms. For β it suffices that ∇_j/τ_j be a well-defined automorphism of S(r) for S = A^{[u,v]}_R, A^{[u,v/p]}_R and 0 ≤ j ≤ d: writing log(1+X)/X = 1 + Σ a_kX^k and X/log(1+X) = 1 + Σ b_kX^k one has v_p(a_k), v_p(b_k) ≥ −k/(p−1), while Lemma 2.34 gives τ^k_j(S(r)) ⊂ π_i^{k(p^{i−1}−δ_R−1)}(p,π_i^{e_0})^kS(r) (using that c^r−1 is divisible by p^2), so the two series of operators converge by the inequality (1 + (p^{i−1}−δ_R−1)/e_0)u > 1/(p−1) and are mutually inverse. For β^c_q one reduces to τ_{i_q}⋯τ_{i_1}∇_0τ^{−1}_0τ^{c,−1}_{i_1}⋯τ^{c,−1}_{i_q} and uses the identity (γ^a_j−1)(γ_0−x) = (γ_0 − xδ(γ^a_j))(γ^{a/c}_j−1) with δ(γ^a_j) = (γ^a_j−1)/(γ^{a/c}_j−1) to show τ_{i_q}⋯τ_{i_1}(γ_0−1)^kτ^{c,−1}_{i_1}⋯τ^{c,−1}_{i_q} ∈ (p^2,γ_0−1,…,γ_d−1)^k, whence convergence of both the operator and its inverse.
items.note: This is where the roots-of-unity hypothesis is used quantitatively. The paper prints the trailing factor of this operator as τ^{c,−1}_{i_1} in four places where τ^{c,−1}_{i_q} is meant (source issue E34).

items.name: Remark 4.7: an integral Lazard isomorphism
items.statement: By Remark 4.3 the isomorphisms of Lemma 4.6 read as a quasi-isomorphism (β,β^c) : RΓ_cont(Γ_R,M) ≅ RΓ(Lie Γ_R,M): a very simple, almost commutative instance of an integral Lazard isomorphism between Lie-algebra and continuous group cohomology for p-adic Lie groups (Huber–Kings–Naumann treat the integral case in general, Tamme an analytic rational version). Setting Laz := (β,β^c) proves Proposition 4.5.

items.name: Lemma 4.8: change of annulus of convergence
items.statement: The natural map Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{(0,v]+}_R(r)) → Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) is a quasi-isomorphism, with no constant. Translating through ι_cycl into analytic functions, it suffices that 1−ϕ : R^{[u,v]}_ϖ/R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ → R^{[u,v/p]}_ϖ/R^{(0,v/p]+}_ϖ be an isomorphism. The natural map between these quotients is an isomorphism (injectivity because a function integral on u/e_0 ≤ v_p(T) ≤ v/e_0 extending integrally to 0 < v_p(T) ≤ v/(pe_0) lies in R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ; surjectivity because r^{[u,v/p]}_{ζ−1} = r^{[u]}_{ζ−1} + r^{(0,v/p]+}_{ζ−1}), and on M := R^{[u,v]}_ϖ/R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ one has ϕ(M) ⊂ pM, so 1−ϕ is invertible once M has no p-divisible elements, which reduces through a topological basis to Laurent expansions in r^{[u,v]}_{ζ−1}/r^{(0,v]+}_{ζ−1}.

items.name: The ψ-Koszul complexes
items.statement: With ℓ := p^{i−1} (so ℓ ≥ ℓ_R), Proposition 2.16 makes π_i^{−ℓ}A^{(0,v]+}_R stable under ψ, and for S = A_R, A^{(0,v]+}_R one sets Kos(ψ,Γ_R,S(r)) to be the 2×2 homotopy limit with rows ψ−1 on Kos(Γ′_R,π_i^{−ℓ}S(r)) and on Kos^c(Γ′_R,π_i^{−ℓ}S(r)) and vertical maps τ_0. For S = A_R there is no difference between π_i^{−ℓ}S and S.

items.name: Proposition 4.9: change of disk of convergence
items.statement: The natural map Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{(0,v]+}_R(r)) → Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A_R(r)) is a p^N-quasi-isomorphism with the safe N=2(p+7), independent of r and n; it is a direct consequence of Lemmas 4.10 and 4.12.
items.note: The printed sharper p^8 bound is not derived by the displayed comparison square. A coarser justified bound suffices for Theorem 4.14; this is a proof gap, not a demonstrated false p^8 claim (E16).

items.name: Lemma 4.10: from ϕ-complexes to ψ-complexes
items.statement: For S = A_R, A^{(0,v]+}_R the natural map Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,S(r)) → Kos(ψ,Γ_R,S(r)), the identity on the first column and ψ on the second, is a p^{p+7}-quasi-isomorphism. The quotient complex is killed by p^2 (Lemma 2.35), and the kernel complex [Kos(Γ′_R,(A^{(0,v/p]+}_R(r))^{ψ=0}) --τ_0--> Kos^c(…)] is p^4-acyclic: by Proposition 2.16 there is a p^{p+1}-isomorphism (A^{(0,v/p]+}_R(r))^{ψ=0} ≅ ⊕_{α≠0} ϕ(A^{(0,v]+}_R)[x^α] with [x^α] = (1+π_i)^{α_0}[x_1^{α_1}]⋯[x_d^{α_d}], and each α is treated separately: if α_k ≠ 0 for some k ≠ 0 then γ_k−1 is injective with cokernel killed by p^2, because (γ_k−1)(ϕ(y)[x^α]) = ϕ(π_1G(y))[x^α] with G invertible (modulo π_1 it is multiplication by α_k); if α_k = 0 for all k ≠ 0 and α_0 ≠ 0 then τ_0 is injective with cokernel killed by p^2, because π_1^{−1}F with F = c^r(1+π_1)^aγ_0 − δ_{i_1}⋯δ_{i_q} and a = p^{−i}(c−1)α_0 ∈ Z_p^* induces multiplication by a on the graded pieces π_i^kA^{(0,v]+}_R/π_i^{k+N}A^{(0,v]+}_R.

items.name: Remark 4.11: the Γ_R-cohomology of the pieces x^αϕ(E^+_R)
items.statement: For α ∈ {0,…,p−1}^{[0,d]} put M_α = x^αϕ(E^+_R). The proof of Lemma 4.10 shows there is N > 0 with (γ_j−1)/π equal to multiplication by α_j on π_i^{pk}M_α/π_i^{pk+pN}M_α for all k ∈ Z; hence for α_j ≠ 0, γ_j−1 is invertible on x^αϕ(E_R) with (γ_j−1)^{−1}π_i^{pk}M_α ⊂ π^{−1}π_i^{pk}M_α, so H^i(Γ_R,π_i^{pk}M_α) is killed by π for all k and all α ≠ 0. Since c_{cycl,α}(π_i^{pk}E^+_R) ⊂ π_i^{pk−δ_R}M_α and x ↦ (c_{cycl,α}(x))_{α≠0} is a Γ_R-equivariant isomorphism E_R^{ψ=0} ≅ ⊕_{α≠0}x^αϕ(E_R), it follows that H^i(Γ_R,(π_i^{pk}E^+_R)^{ψ=0}) is killed by ππ_i^{δ_R} for all k ∈ Z and all i.
items.note: This is the quantitative input to the decompletion argument of Proposition 4.13(iii).

items.name: Lemma 4.12: the ψ-complexes on a disk and on A_R agree
items.statement: The natural map Kos(ψ,Γ_R,A^{(0,v]+}_R(r)) → Kos(ψ,Γ_R,A_R(r)) is a quasi-isomorphism. It is injective, and since A_R is the p-adic completion of A^{(0,v]+}_R[π_i^{−1}], Proposition 2.16 makes ψ pointwise topologically nilpotent on A_R/π_i^{−ℓ}A^{(0,v]+}_R, so 1−ψ is bijective there and hence on the two Koszul complexes of the quotient.

items.name: The rings of the Galois comparison and Abhyankar descent
items.statement: ~R_∞ is the integral closure of R in the sub-R[1/p]-algebra of R̄[1/p] generated by ζ_m and X_{a+b+1}^{1/m},…,X_d^{1/m} for all m ≥ 1, so R_∞ ⊂ ~R_∞, and by Abhyankar's lemma R̄ is the maximal extension of ~R_∞ étale in characteristic zero. ~Γ_R := Gal(~R_∞[1/p]/R[1/p]) has Γ_R as a quotient with kernel Γ_1 ≅ ∏_{ℓ≠p}(Z_ℓ(1))^c, of order prime to p. The spectral completion C(~R_∞[1/p]) is perfectoid, E_{~R_∞} is the tilt of that completion, E^+_{~R_∞} its ring of integers, and A_{~R_∞} = W(E_{~R_∞}) = A_{R̄}^{Gal(R̄[1/p]/~R_∞[1/p])}.
items.note: Make the completion explicit, consistently with C(S) in §2.4.1. Perfectoid algebras are complete; the algebraic tower union is not silently identified with its completion.

items.name: Proposition 4.13: Artin–Schreier, almost étale descent, decompletion
items.statement: (i) The Artin–Schreier sequence 0 → Z_p → A_{R̄} --1−ϕ--> A_{R̄} → 0 induces a quasi-isomorphism RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)) ≅ [RΓ_cont(G_R,A_{R̄}(r)) --1−ϕ--> RΓ_cont(G_R,A_{R̄}(r))]. (ii) The inclusions A_{R_∞} ⊂ A_{~R_∞} ⊂ A_{R̄} induce quasi-isomorphisms µ_H : RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_{R_∞}(r)) ≅ RΓ_cont(~Γ_R,A_{~R_∞}(r)) ≅ RΓ_cont(G_R,A_{R̄}(r)) — the first because Γ_1 has order prime to p, the second by almost étale descent. (iii) The inclusion A_R ⊂ A_{R_∞} induces a quasi-isomorphism µ_∞ : RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_R(r)) ≅ RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_{R_∞}(r)), proved by decompletion: modulo p one has E_R = ϕ(E_R) ⊕ E_R^{ψ=0} iterated, so every x ∈ ϕ^{−∞}(E_R) is uniquely s_0(x) + Σ_{n≥1}s^*_n(x) with s^*_n(x) ∈ ϕ^{−n}(E_R^{ψ=0}); the normalised traces s_n = ϕ^{−n}∘ψ^k∘ϕ^{n+k} are a uniform family of uniformly continuous maps by Proposition 2.16(ii), so they extend to E_{R_∞} and give a Γ_R-equivariant splitting E_{R_∞} = E_R ⊕ Z; Remark 4.11 then makes every continuous cocycle on Z a coboundary, whence H^i(Γ_R,Z) = 0.
items.note: Almost étale descent is quoted from Colmez, Andreatta–Brinon and Andreatta–Iovita; the decompletion technique from Andreatta–Iovita [4, Theorem 7.16] and Kedlaya–Liu [37], though (iii) is proved here in the form needed.

items.name: Theorem 4.14: the local period map is a quasi-isomorphism
items.statement: Assume K contains enough roots of unity. There are universal constants N and c_p and p^{Nr+c_p}-quasi-isomorphisms α^Laz_r : τ^{≤r}Syn(R,r) ≅ τ^{≤r}RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)) and α^Laz_{r,n} : τ^{≤r}Syn(R,r)_n ≅ τ^{≤r}RΓ_cont(G_R,Z/p^n(r)). The proof is the composite: Syn(R,r) ≅ Cycl(R^{[u,v]}_ϖ,r) (§3, in degrees ≤ r); ≅ Kos(ϕ,∂,F^rA^{[u,v]}_R) (§4.1); τ^{≤r}(·) ≅ τ^{≤r}Kos(ϕ,Lie Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) (Lemma 4.4, the only place truncation is unavoidable); ≅ Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{[u,v]}_R(r)) (Proposition 4.5); ≅ Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A^{(0,v]+}_R(r)) ≅ Kos(ψ,Γ_R,A^{(0,v]+}_R(r)) ≅ Kos(ψ,Γ_R,A_R(r)) ≅ Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A_R(r)) (Lemmas 4.8, 4.10, 4.12); ≅ [RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_R(r)) --1−ϕ--> RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_R(r))] (§4.2); ≅ RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)) (Proposition 4.13).
items.note: Theorem 1.6 of the introduction states the same result with the constant p^{Nr}; here it is p^{Nr+c_p}. The further identification with étale cohomology of the affinoid uses the K(π,1)-lemma and Abhyankar, which are in §5, not §4.

items.name: Remark 4.15: earlier Koszul descriptions of Galois cohomology
items.statement: Quasi-isomorphisms Kos(ϕ,Γ_R,A_R(r)) ≅ RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)) of this type were obtained before for local fields with imperfect residue fields by Morita (torsion coefficients) and Zerbes (rational coefficients), and for perfect residue field with a complex similar to the case d = 1 by Tavares Ribeiro; all are generalisations of the complex of Herr's thesis.

items.name: The local Fontaine–Messing period map α̃^FM_{r,n}
items.statement: Let E^PD_{R,n} be the log-PD envelope of R_n in A_cr(R̄)_n ⊗ R^+_ϖ compatible with the PD structures on A_{cr,n} and O_F; then E^PD_{R,n} = E^PD_R/p^n carries a G_R-action (trivial on R^+_ϖ) and a Frobenius compatible with ϕ_Kum. With Ω_{E^PD_{R,n}} := E^PD_{R,n} ⊗_{R^+_{ϖ,n}} Ω_{R^+_{ϖ,n}} and the filtration F^rΩ^•_{E^PD_{R,n}}, the Fontaine–Messing period map is the composite α̃^FM_{r,n} : Syn(R,r)_n = [F^rΩ^•_{R^PD_{ϖ,n}} --p^r−p^•ϕ--> Ω^•_{R^PD_{ϖ,n}}] → C(G_R,[F^rΩ^•_{E^PD_{R,n}} --p^r−p^•ϕ--> Ω^•_{E^PD_{R,n}}]) ← C(G_R,[F^rA_cr(R̄)_n --p^r−ϕ--> A_cr(R̄)_n]) ← C(G_R,Z/p^n(r)′), where the second quasi-isomorphism is the Poincaré lemma F^rA_cr(R̄)_n ≅ F^rΩ^•_{E^PD_{R,n}} of Tsuji [63, Lemma 3.1.7] (compare Lemma 2.37) and the third is the fundamental exact sequence of Lemma 2.23(ii).
items.note: The source must be R^PD_ϖ as in §3.1; the fat ring belongs to the target cochain construction (E17).

items.name: Theorem 4.16: the two period maps agree
items.statement: If K has enough roots of unity then α̃^FM_{r,n} is p^{Nr+c_p}-equal to α̃^Laz_{r,n} of Theorem 4.14, for the same universal constants. The proof is a seven-row commutative diagram: its first row is the Fontaine–Messing chain, its lower boundary the Lazard chain, and the vertical maps are the injection R^PD_ϖ ⊂ R^{[u,v]}_ϖ, inflation from Γ_R to G_R along R_∞ ⊂ R̄ (a quasi-isomorphism by almost étale descent, i.e. Faltings' purity or its extensions by Scholze or Kedlaya–Liu), the inclusion R ⊂ R_∞ (a quasi-isomorphism by decompletion, though this is not needed), the maps λ of §4.2 from continuous cohomology to Koszul complexes, the maps Laz of Lemma 4.6 and Remark 4.7, and the multiplications by powers of t from Lemma 4.4; the horizontal comparisons are the Poincaré lemmas of Lemma 2.37 and Lemma 3.11 and the fundamental exact sequences of Lemma 2.23.
items.note: 'p^{Nr+c_p}-equal' is not among the notions of Definition 1.13; it means that the difference of the two maps on cohomology is annihilated by p^{Nr+c_p}.

items.name: The three base log structures
items.statement: Working in the category of integral quasi-coherent log-schemes, O_K, O^×_K and O^0_K denote Spec(O_K) with, respectively, the trivial log structure, the canonical one (associated to the closed point) and the one given by (N → O_K, 1 ↦ 0). C := K̄^∧.

items.name: Absolute log-crystalline and syntomic complexes and the sheaves 𝒮_n(r)
items.statement: For X log-smooth over O^×_K and r ≥ 0, the absolute (over O_F) log-crystalline complexes are RΓ_cr(X,J^{[r]})_n := RΓ(X_ét, Ru_{X_n/W_n(k)*}J^{[r]}_{X_n/W_n(k)}) and RΓ_cr(X,J^{[r]}) := holim_n of these, with J^{[r]} := O for r ≤ 0 by convention. The syntomic complexes are RΓ_syn(X,r)_n := [RΓ_cr(X,J^{[r]})_n --p^r−ϕ--> RΓ_cr(X_n)] and RΓ_syn(X,r) := holim_n, the Frobenius being the composite through RΓ_cr(X_1/O_F)_n; the mapping fibres are taken in the ∞-derived category of abelian groups. One has RΓ_syn(X,r)_n ≅ RΓ_syn(X,r) ⊗^L Z/p^n and a canonical quasi-isomorphism RΓ_syn(X,r)_n ≅ [RΓ_cr(X)_n --(p^r−ϕ,can)--> RΓ_cr(X)_n ⊕ RΓ_cr(X,O/J^{[r]})_n]. Sheafifying the presheaves U ↦ RΓ_cr(U,J^{[r]})_n, RΓ_cr(U)_n, RΓ_syn(U,r)_n on the étale site gives J^{[r]}_{cr,n}, A_{cr,n} and 𝒮_n(r), with 𝒮_n(r) ≅ [J^{[r]}_{cr,n} --p^r−ϕ--> A_{cr,n}] and RΓ_syn(X,r)_n = RΓ(X_ét,𝒮_n(r)).

items.name: Remark 5.1: the log-syntomic site and the twists S_n(r)
items.statement: Equivalently, syntomic cohomology is the cohomology of the log-syntomic site: for fine log-schemes, the objects of the small site X_syn are morphisms that are log-syntomic in Kato's sense (integral, flat and locally of finite presentation on underlying schemes, and étale-locally factoring as an exact closed immersion transversally regular over the base followed by a log-smooth morphism), required in addition to be locally quasi-finite with torsion cokernel on log structures. For X log-syntomic over Spec W(k) put O^cr_n(X) = H^0_cr(X,O)_n and J^{[r]}_n(X) = H^0_cr(X,J^{[r]})_n; the presheaves J^{[r]}_n are sheaves on X_{n,syn}, flat over Z/p^n, with J^{[r]}_{n+1} ⊗ Z/p^n ≅ J^{[r]}_n and RΓ(X_syn,J^{[r]}_n) ≅ RΓ_cr(X,J^{[r]})_n compatibly with Frobenius. The syntomic Tate twist is S_n(r) := [J^{[r]}_n --p^r−ϕ--> O^cr_n], extended to X_syn by the exact pushforward i_*, and 𝒮_n(r) = Rε_*S_n(r) for ε : X_syn → X_ét, so RΓ_syn(X,r)_n = RΓ(X_ét,𝒮_n(r)) = RΓ(X_syn,S_n(r)).
items.note: The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: The Frobenius-eigenspace presentation of 𝒮_n(r)
items.statement: For X semistable over O_K or a base change of such, Proposition 3.12 gives 𝒮_n(r) ≅ [J^{[r]}_{cr,n} --p^r−ϕ--> A_{cr,n}] ≅ [A^{ϕ=p^r}_{cr,n} → A_{cr,n}/J^{[r]}_{cr,n}], where A^{ϕ=p^r}_{cr,n} := [A_{cr,n} --p^r−ϕ--> A_{cr,n}].

items.name: Corollary 5.2: torsion bounds for the syntomic sheaves
items.statement: For X semistable over O_K or a base change of such: (i) for i ≠ r the sheaf H^i(A^{ϕ=p^r}_{cr,n}) is annihilated by p^N for a constant N = N(e,d,p,r); (ii) for i ≥ r+1 the sheaf H^i(𝒮_n(r)) is annihilated by p^{N(r)}; (iii) for i ≤ r−1 the natural map H^{i−1}(A_{cr,n}/J^{[r]}_{cr,n}) → H^i(𝒮_n(r)) is a p^N-isomorphism for a constant N = N(e,d,p,r), and there is a p^N-exact sequence 0 → H^{r−1}(A_{cr,n}/J^{[r]}_{cr,n}) → H^r(𝒮_n(r)) → H^r(A^{ϕ=p^r}_{cr,n}) → 0.
items.note: Deduced from Proposition 3.12. The paper prints the displayed sequence as exact although the maps it needs to kill are only controlled up to p^N by part (i) (source issue E37).

items.name: Theorem 5.4: syntomic sheaves compute p-adic nearby cycles
items.statement: Let X be a scheme with semistable reduction over O_K, or a base change of a scheme with semistable reduction over the ring of integers of a subfield of K, and for 0 ≤ i ≤ r consider α^FM_{r,n} : H^i(𝒮_n(r)_X) → i^*R^ij_*Z/p^n(r)′_{X_tr}. (i) If K has enough roots of unity, the kernel and cokernel are annihilated by p^{Nr+c_p} for universal constants N and c_p. (ii) In general they are annihilated by p^N for an integer N = N(K,p,r) depending on K, p and r. The proof is local: for A as in (5.3) with Spec(A/p) connected, RΓ_syn(Spec A,r)_n = Syn(Â,r)_n, and α^FM_{r,n} factors as the henselian version of α̃^FM_{r,n} followed by C(G_R,Z/p^n(r)′) → RΓ(Y_{tr,ét},Z/p^n(r)′) for R = A^h; one passes to the completion by the diagram (5.6), in which the middle vertical map is an isomorphism by Lemma 5.8 (Abhyankar plus Elkik), the map f by the K(π,1)-lemma of §5.1.4 and the map g by the rigid GAGA argument of §5.1.5; then Theorems 4.14 and 4.16 give (i). For (ii) one passes to R_i := R(ζ_{p^i}) with i ≥ c(K)+3, which has enough roots of unity, and descends along G_i = Gal(K_i/K) using Lemma 5.9.
items.note: Theorem 1.1(ii) records N(e,p,r); the N(K,p,r) formulation here is weaker, not contradictory. E1 is rejected as an error claim; uniform descent remains an implementation obligation.

items.name: The local-to-global diagrams (5.5) and (5.6)
items.statement: (5.5) is the factorisation α^FM_{r,n} : H^iSyn(A,r)_n --α̃^FM_{r,n}--> H^iC(G_R,Z/p^n(r)′) → H^iRΓ(Y_{tr,ét},Z/p^n(r)′) for i ≤ r, R = A^h, Y = Spec A^h. (5.6) is the commutative square comparing this with its completed version: the rows are H^i(Syn(A,r)_n) → H^i(G_R,Z/p^n(r)′) → H^i(U_ét,Z/p^n(r)′) and H^i(Syn(Â,r)_n) → H^i(G_R̂,Z/p^n(r)′) → H^i(Ū_ét,Z/p^n(r)′), with U = (Spec R)_tr and Ū = (Sp R̂[1/p])_tr; the middle vertical is an isomorphism by Lemma 5.8, f by the K(π,1)-lemma and g by rigid GAGA.

items.name: Theorem 5.7: Riemann's existence theorem
items.statement: (Riemann's Existence) Let X be a smooth quasi-compact rigid space, Z ⊂ X a normal crossings divisor and U = X ∖ Z. Then any finite étale covering of U extends uniquely to a finite flat normal covering of X. This is the main theorem of Lütkebohmert; the proof passes to pointed disks through Kiehl's description of tubular neighbourhoods and then applies Lütkebohmert's extension lemma.
items.note: Quoted from Lütkebohmert; it is what makes the Galois-to-étale comparison available for formal schemes in §5.2.3. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Lemma 5.8: Abhyankar's lemma and Elkik approximation
items.statement: Let R be as in (5.3), or a henselisation at (p) of such a ring, or a ring as in §2.2.2; let R_m := R(ζ_m)[X_{a+b+1}^{1/m},…,X_d^{1/m}], R′_∞ := ∪_m R_m, and R̄′_∞ the maximal extension of R′_∞ étale in characteristic zero. (i) (Abhyankar) The inclusion R̄′_∞ ⊂ R̄ is an equality, so G_R = Gal(R̄[1/p]/R[1/p]) ≅ Gal(R̄′_∞[1/p]/R[1/p]). (ii) (Approximation) For R a henselisation of a ring of the form (5.3), the natural map G_R̂ → G_R is an isomorphism. The proof of (i) uses Abhyankar's lemma in SGA 1 for the regular ring R[1/p] — and, in the affinoid case, the existence of the covering space from Theorem 5.7; (ii) reduces to Gal(R̂̄_m[1/p]/R̂_m[1/p]) ≅ Gal(R̄_m[1/p]/R_m[1/p]) for each m, which is Elkik's approximation theorem since R_m is henselian at (p) with completion R̂_m.

items.name: The K(π,1)-lemma for the trivialised locus of an affinoid
items.statement: The map f of (5.6) is an isomorphism: the K(π,1)-property holds for Ū = (Sp R̂[1/p])_tr with p-power coefficients. For trivial divisor at infinity this is Scholze's theorem; the general case follows Faltings' treatment of the algebraic case. One must show that any class β ∈ H^i(Ū_ét,M), i > 0, with M locally constant constructible p^n-torsion, dies in a finite étale extension of Ū. By Lemma 5.8 one may, after adjoining k-th roots of the equations of the divisor and roots of unity, assume M unramified; then the Leray spectral sequence E^{s,t}_2 = H^s(Sp(R̂[1/p])_ét,R^tj_*M) ⇒ H^{s+t}(Ū_ét,M) has the property that taking p^k-th roots of f = the product of those equations induces multiplication by p^{tk} on E^{s,t}_2, by log purity (de Jong–van der Put, Nakayama): R^tj_*Z/p^n ≅ ∧^tM̄^{gp}_Y ⊗ Z/p^n(−t) for Y = Sp(R̂[1/p]) with its log structure M_Y = j_*O^*_Ū ∩ O_Y. Repeating reduces β to a class on Sp(R̂[1/p]), where Scholze's lemma applies again.
items.note: The paper prints the purity formula with the twist (−1) instead of (−t), correct only for t = 1 (source issue E20). The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: The rigid GAGA comparison
items.statement: The map g of (5.6) is an isomorphism: H^i(U_ét,Z/p^n) ≅ H^i(Ū_ét,Z/p^n) for U = (Spec R)_tr and Ū its rigid analytic avatar. Induction on the number s of irreducible components of the divisor D_K: for s = 0 this is Gabber's affine analogue of the proper base change theorem, and the inductive step compares the localisation sequences of étale and rigid étale cohomology (de Jong–van der Put), whose outer terms are isomorphic by induction.
items.note: The paper prints the localisation sequence with the first term in degree i instead of i−2 (and with the twists omitted), which cannot be right with a Gysin map to degree i and a boundary map to degree i−1 (source issue E21). The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Lemma 5.9: ramified Galois descent for syntomic cohomology
items.statement: Let K_1/K be Galois with relative ramification index e_1 and group G, and R_1 := R ⊗_{O_K} O_{K_1}. The natural map RΓ_syn(R,r) → RΓ(G,RΓ_syn(R_1,r)) is a p^{cre_1}-quasi-isomorphism for a universal constant c. Étale descent for crystalline cohomology reduces to the totally ramified case; writing RΓ_syn(R,r) = [RΓ_cr(R)^{ϕ=p^r} → RΓ_cr(R)/F^r] it suffices to treat the two factors. For the Frobenius factor one factors the m-th power of Frobenius (p^m ≥ e) through the special fibre and uses that ϕ^m is a p^{2rm}-quasi-isomorphism on the eigenspaces, so both maps in the factorisation are p^{4rm}-quasi-isomorphisms. For the filtration factor one uses Beilinson's identification of filtered log-crystalline cohomology with the filtered derived log de Rham complex, and Nekovář–Nizioł's comparison RΓ_cr(R)_n/F^r → RΓ_dR(R/O_K)_n/F^r, reducing to Ω^•_{R_1/O_{K_1}} = Ω^•_{R/O_K} ⊗_{O_K} O_{K_1}.
items.note: The source assertion p^(c r e_1) is retained as an unclosed proof obligation. The proof’s scalar and K_0 notation are corrected in E22; coarser estimates do not disprove the lemma.

items.name: Remark 5.10: the explicit Galois action on the coordinate ring
items.statement: The G-action on RΓ_syn(R_1,r) and the map from RΓ_syn(R,r) can be seen explicitly by replacing the coordinate ring O_F[T_1] of O_{K_1} (T_1 ↦ ϖ_1) with O_F[T,X_σ : σ ∈ G], T ↦ ϖ, X_σ ↦ σ(ϖ_1), on which g ∈ G acts by g(T) = T and g(X_σ) = X_{gσ}.

items.name: Corollary 5.11: de Rham cohomology computes rigid étale cohomology
items.statement: For 𝔛 a quasi-compact formal semistable scheme over O_K and α_{r,i} : H^{i−1}_dR(𝔛_{K,tr}) → H^i_syn(𝔛,r)_Q --α^FM_r--> H^i_ét(𝔛_{K,tr},Q_p(r)): for i ≤ r−1 the map α_{r,i} is an isomorphism, and α_{r,r} is injective.
items.note: Corollary 1.4 adds that the cokernel of α_{r,r} can be very large when dim 𝔛_K ≥ 1, and identifies α_{r,i} with the Bloch–Kato exponential in the proper case. The cross-reference to 'section 2.1.2' for the local form is wrong; the paper has no §2.1.2 and means §2.2.2 (source issue E19).

items.name: Geometric log-crystalline and syntomic cohomology
items.statement: For X log-smooth over O^×_K and universally saturated, RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄},J^{[r]})_n, its homotopy limit and its rationalisation are defined as in the arithmetic case over O_K̄. If X is proper then RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄}) is a perfect A_cr-complex with RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄})_n ≅ RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄}) ⊗^L_{A_cr} A_cr/p^n ≅ RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄}) ⊗^L Z/p^n (Beilinson); in general RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄},J^{[r]})_n ≅ RΓ_cr(X_{O_K̄},J^{[r]}) ⊗^L Z/p^n, and F^rA_cr = RΓ_cr(Spec O_K̄,J^{[r]}) (Tsuji). The geometric syntomic complexes RΓ_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_n, RΓ_syn(X_{O_K̄},r), RΓ_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q and the sheaves 𝒮(r), 𝒮_n(r) are defined by the same formulas.

items.name: Corollary 5.12: the geometric comparison
items.statement: (i) For X semistable over O_K or a base change of such, and 0 ≤ j ≤ r, the kernel and cokernel of α^FM_{r,n} : H^j(𝒮_n(r)_{X_{O_K̄}}) → ī^*R^j j̄_*Z/p^n(r)′_{X_K̄} are annihilated by p^{Nr} for a universal constant N. (ii) For X a proper fine and saturated log-scheme log-smooth over O^×_K, α^FM_r : H^j_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q ≅ H^j(X_{tr,K̄},Q_p(r)) for j ≤ r. Part (i) follows from Theorem 5.4 by passing to the limit over finite extensions of K; naive syntomic cohomology may be replaced by the real one because the finite-coefficient étale groups are finite, so the derived limits vanish; and the passage from semistable to general log-smooth X uses T. Saito's semistable model after a ramified base change together with the invariance of syntomic cohomology under log blow-ups.
items.note: This is (1.8)/(1.9) of the introduction, and recovers Tsuji's Theorem 3.3.4.

items.name: The syntomic fibre sequence over HK and de Rham, algebraic case
items.statement: For X proper and semistable over O_K with no multiplicities in the special fibre, Nekovář–Nizioł give (5.13) RΓ_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q = [[RΓ_HK(X) ⊗_F B^+_st]^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} --ι_dR--> (RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r], where RΓ_HK(X) ≅ RΓ_cr(X_0/O^0_F)_Q is Beilinson's Hyodo–Kato cohomology, ι_dR the Hyodo–Kato map attached to ϖ, and [·]^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} is the homotopy limit of the square with rows 1−ϕ/p^r and 1−ϕ/p^{r−1} and vertical maps N. On cohomology H^j[RΓ_HK(X) ⊗_F B^+_st]^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} = (H^j_HK(X) ⊗_F B^+_st)^{ϕ=p^r,N=0}, and by Hodge–de Rham degeneration H^j((RΓ_dR(X_K) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r) = (H^j_dR(X_K) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r; whence the long exact sequence (5.14) → (H^{j−1}_dR ⊗ B^+_dR)/F^r → H^j_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q → (H^j_HK ⊗ B^+_st)^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} → (H^j_dR ⊗ B^+_dR)/F^r →
items.note: The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Corollary 5.15: the semistable conjecture for log-schemes
items.statement: (Semistable conjecture) For X proper, fine and saturated, log-smooth over O^×_K with Cartier type reduction, there is a natural B_st-linear Galois-equivariant period isomorphism α : H^i(X_{tr,K̄},Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_st ≅ H^i_HK(X) ⊗_F B_st preserving Frobenius and monodromy, which after extension to B_dR induces a filtered isomorphism α : H^i(X_{tr,K̄},Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR ≅ H^i_dR(X_K) ⊗_K B_dR. For r ≥ i the map is the composite of α^FM_r (an isomorphism by Corollary 5.12) with the projections to the Hyodo–Kato term, and what has to be proved is that the triple D^i = (H^i_HK(X),H^i_dR(X_K),ι_dR) is admissible with H^i(X_{tr,K̄},Q_p) ≅ V_st(D^i), which is Proposition 5.20.
items.note: The proof writes 'H^i_dR(X_K) is admissible' and V_st(H^i_dR(X_K)) where the triple D^i is meant (source issue E36).

items.name: Finite dimensional Banach Spaces and their Dimension
items.statement: A Banach Space is a functor Λ ↦ W(Λ) from sympathetic algebras (spectral Banach algebras on which x ↦ x^p is surjective on {|x−1| < 1}; such an algebra is in particular perfectoid) to Q_p-Banach spaces; a sequence of Banach Spaces is exact when it is exact on every Λ. Trivial examples: a finite dimensional Q_p-vector space V with Λ ↦ V, and V_d with V_d(Λ) = Λ^d. W is finite dimensional if there are finite dimensional Q_p-vector spaces V_1, V_2 and exact sequences 0 → V_1 → Y → V_d → 0 and 0 → V_2 → Y → W → 0; then dim W := d and ht W := dim_{Q_p}V_1 − dim_{Q_p}V_2, and Dim W := (dim W, ht W) ∈ N × Z. Morally W is a d-dimensional C-vector space up to a finite dimensional Q_p-vector space. (In Colmez's paper dim is the 'dimension principale', ht the 'dimension résiduelle'.)
items.note: Quoted from Colmez, Espaces de Banach de dimension finie; the atlas plans Banach–Colmez geometry at VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Proposition 5.16: the Dimension calculus
items.statement: (i) The Dimension of a finite dimensional Banach Space does not depend on the choices in its definition. (ii) For a morphism f : W_1 → W_2 of finite dimensional Banach Spaces, Ker f, Coker f and Im f are finite dimensional and Dim W_1 = Dim Ker f + Dim Im f, Dim W_2 = Dim Coker f + Dim Im f. (iii) If dim W = 0 then ht W ≥ 0. (iv) If W has an increasing filtration with successive quotients V_1, and W′ ⊂ W is a sub-Banach Space, then ht W′ ≥ 0.
items.note: (i) and (ii) are the core of Colmez's theory (his Theorem 0.4), (iii) is immediate and (iv) is Colmez's Lemme 2.6 in the Astérisque paper; none is proved here. The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Corollary 5.17: maps into Dimension-zero Spaces vanish
items.statement: (i) If W_1 is a successive extension of V_1's and dim W_2 = 0, then every morphism W_1 → W_2 is zero. (ii) Let W_1, W_2 be finite dimensional with W_i = W_i(C), W_2 a successive extension of V_1's, and let f : W_1 → W_2 be a Q_p-linear map lifting to a morphism of Banach Spaces; if either dim_{Q_p}Coker f < ∞, or dim_{Q_p}Ker f < ∞ and dim W_1 = dim W_2, then f is surjective. (iii) If the kernel and cokernel of f_C are finite dimensional over Q_p then dim W_1 = dim W_2. The proof of (i): dim Im f = 0 and ht W_1 = 0 give ht Im f = −ht Ker f ≤ 0 by 5.16(iv), so Im f = 0.

items.name: Example 5.18: the Spaces X^r_st(D) and X^r_dR(D)
items.statement: Let D = (D_st,D_dR,λ) with D_st a finite dimensional F-vector space with bijective semilinear ϕ and linear N satisfying Nϕ = pϕN, D_dR a finite dimensional filtered K-vector space (decreasing, separated, exhaustive, indexed by N) and λ : D_st → D_dR F-linear. For r ∈ N set X^r_st(D) := (t^{−r}B^+_st ⊗_F D_st)^{ϕ=1,N=0} and X^r_dR(D) := (t^{−r}B^+_dR ⊗_K D_dR)/F^0; these are the C-points of finite dimensional Banach Spaces with Dim X^r_dR(D) = (r dim_K D_dR − Σ_{i=1}^r dim F^iD_dR, 0) and Dim X^r_st(D) = Σ_{r_i≤r}(r−r_i,1) for r_i the slopes of ϕ with multiplicity. If F^{r+1}D_dR = 0 and all r_i ≤ r — r(D) being the least such r — then Dim X^r_st(D) = (r dim_F D_st − t_N(D_st), dim_F D_st) and Dim X^r_dR(D) = (r dim_K D_dR − t_H(D_dR), 0), where t_N(D) = v_p(det ϕ) and t_H(D) = Σ_{i≥0} i·dim_K(F^iD_dR/F^{i+1}D_dR). The map λ extends to X^r_st(D) → X^r_dR(D), and if λ : K ⊗_F D_st → D_dR is bijective (rk D := dim_F D_st = dim_K D_dR) the kernel on C-points is V_st(D) for r ≥ r(D).
items.note: The Dimension formulas are Colmez's Proposition 0.8 and the identification of the kernel his Proposition 10.14. The paper prints all four formulas with lowercase 'dim' although the right-hand sides are pairs (source issue E35). The former owner covers only a proper sub-contract; the complete item remains missing pending the route revision.

items.name: Lemma 5.19: a Banach-Space form of "weakly admissible implies admissible"
items.statement: If λ : K ⊗_F D_st → D_dR is an isomorphism and t_H(D_dR) = t_N(D_st), the following are equivalent: (i) V_st(D) is finite dimensional over Q_p; (ii) X^r_st(D) → X^r_dR(D) is surjective for r = r(D); (ii′) the same for all r ≥ r(D). They imply (iii) t_N(D′) ≥ t_H(D′) for every D′ ⊂ D stable under ϕ and N, that is, D is weakly admissible; and (iv) dim_{Q_p}V_st(D) = rk D. The hypothesis gives dim X^r_dR(D) = dim X^r_st(D) for r ≥ r(D), and X^r_dR(D) is a successive extension of V_1's, so Corollary 5.17(ii) applies; (iii) follows because a subobject with t_N < t_H would make the kernel of dimension ≥ 1 and V_st infinite dimensional.

items.name: Proposition 5.20: from the syntomic sequences to admissibility
items.statement: Suppose given, for r ∈ N, triples D^i = (D^i_st,D^i_dR,λ_i) as above with F^{i+1}D^i_dR = 0, and long exact sequences ⋯ → H^i(r) → X^r_st(D^i) → X^r_dR(D^i) → H^{i+1}(r) → ⋯ with dim_{Q_p}H^i(r) finite for r ≥ i. Then (i) λ_i : K ⊗_F D^i_st → D^i_dR is bijective for i ≥ 0; (ii) D^i is weakly admissible; (iii) X^r_st(D^i) → X^r_dR(D^i) is surjective for r ≥ i; (iv) H^i(r) = V_st(D^i) for r ≥ i. The proof: finiteness of H^i(r), H^{i+1}(r) and Corollary 5.17(iii) give dim X^r_dR(D^i) = dim X^r_st(D^i), hence dim_F D^i_st = dim_K D^i_dR and t_H = t_N; the image D′ = Im λ_i has X^r_dR(D^i/D′) = 0, so λ_i is bijective; (ii) is then Lemma 5.19, and r(D^i) ≤ i by the Hodge hypothesis; finally for i ≤ r−1 the map X^r_dR(D^i) → H^{i+1}(r) vanishes by Corollary 5.17(i), which splits the long exact sequence.
items.note: This is the engine of both semistable conjectures, Corollaries 5.15 and 5.26.

items.name: Syntomic cohomology of formal log-schemes and the rigid period map
items.statement: For 𝔛 a fine log p-adic formal scheme, log-smooth over O^×_K and universally saturated, the arithmetic and geometric syntomic cohomologies are defined by the same formulas as in the algebraic case. For 𝔛 semistable over O_K there is a rigid analytic Fontaine–Messing map α^FM_{r,n} : H^j_syn(𝔛,r)_n → H^j(𝔛_{K,tr},Z/p^n(r)′), defined as in Tsuji's algebraic case: cover 𝔛 by affine formal schemes of the standard presentation, apply the local map α̃^FM_{r,n} : Syn(R,r)_n → C(G_R,Z/p^n(r)′) on each, use the quasi-isomorphism C(G_R,Z/p^n(r)′) ≅ RΓ((Sp R[1/p])_{tr,ét},Z/p^n(r)′) — obtained from Theorem 5.7 by the Abhyankar argument of Lemma 5.8 — to pass to a Čech complex of étale cohomology, and descend.

items.name: Corollary 5.21: syntomic equals étale for proper semistable formal schemes
items.statement: For 𝔛 a proper semistable formal scheme over O_K the period map α^FM_r : H^j_syn(𝔛_{O_K̄},r)_Q ≅ H^j(𝔛_{K̄,tr},Q_p(r)) is an isomorphism for j ≤ r. The proof passes to the limit over finite extensions of K from the mod-p^n statement, and replaces naive by genuine syntomic cohomology because the groups H^*(𝔛_{K̄,tr},Z/p^n(r)) are finite by Scholze's finiteness theorem, so the relevant higher derived limits vanish.
items.note: The proof passes through a finite-coefficient comparison before the rational statement. Its first/second/final-claim wording is not evidence that a theorem should be inserted. The formal local comparison and derived-limit passage must be proved.

items.name: Hyodo–Kato cohomology of a formal scheme
items.statement: For 𝔛_1 of Cartier type over Spec(O_{K,1})^×, RΓ_HK(𝔛) ≅ RΓ_cr(𝔛_0/O^0_F)_Q, and Beilinson gives the quasi-isomorphisms (RΓ_HK(𝔛) ⊗_F B^+_st)^{N=0} ≅ RΓ_HK(𝔛) ⊗_F B^+_cr and ι_cr : RΓ_HK(𝔛) ⊗_F B^+_cr ≅ RΓ_cr(𝔛)_Q, compatible with N and ϕ, together with the Hyodo–Kato isomorphism ι_dR : RΓ_HK(𝔛) ⊗_F K ≅ RΓ_dR(𝔛_K); for 𝔛 semistable RΓ_dR(𝔛_K) ≅ RΓ_dR(𝔛_{K,tr}), so ι_dR lands in RΓ_dR(𝔛_{K,tr}). The complex RΓ_HK(𝔛) is built from finite rank (ϕ,N)-modules over F.
items.note: The Hyodo–Kato isomorphism is quoted from Beilinson.

items.name: Proposition 5.22: the syntomic fibre sequence for formal schemes
items.statement: For 𝔛 proper and semistable over O_K with Cartier type reduction: (i) (5.23) RΓ_syn(𝔛_{O_K̄},r)_Q ≅ [[RΓ_HK(𝔛) ⊗_F B^+_st]^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} --ι_dR--> (RΓ_dR(𝔛_K) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r]; (ii) for j < r there are short exact sequences (5.24) 0 → H^j_syn(𝔛_{O_K̄},r)_Q → (H^j_HK(𝔛) ⊗_F B^+_st)^{ϕ=p^r,N=0} → (H^j_dR(𝔛_K) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r → 0. The proof introduces the completed derived log de Rham complexes RΓ^♮_dR(𝔛_{O_K̄}) with A_dR := LΩ^{•,∧}_{O_K̄/O_K} = RΓ^♮_dR(O^×_K̄), whose filtered pieces are acyclic in nonzero degrees with lim_F A_dR ⊗̂ Q_p = B^+_dR; Nekovář–Nizioł's κ_r identifies RΓ_cr(𝔛_{O_K̄})_Q/F^r with RΓ^♮_dR(𝔛_{O_K̄}) ⊗̂ Q_p/F^r, and γ_r identifies (RΓ_dR(𝔛_K) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r with it; the identification of the Frobenius eigenspace uses ι_cr and the commuting triangle of [46, Lemma 3.23]. For (ii) the cohomology groups H^j((RΓ_dR(𝔛_K) ⊗_K B^+_dR)/F^r) are finite dimensional Banach Spaces that are successive extensions of V_1 (being finite length B^+_dR-modules), and the splitting follows as in Proposition 5.20 because H^j_syn(𝔛_{O_K̄},r)_Q is a finite dimensional Q_p-vector space for j ≤ r by Corollary 5.21; the identification of H^j((RΓ_dR ⊗ B^+_dR)/F^r) with (H^j_dR ⊗ B^+_dR)/F^r for j < r follows from Hodge–de Rham degeneration — itself a consequence of Scholze's de Rham comparison for proper rigid spaces — or directly from (5.24) and the F^r-triangle.

items.name: Corollary 5.26: the semistable conjecture for formal schemes
items.statement: (Semistable conjecture) For 𝔛 a proper semistable formal scheme over O_K there is a natural B_st-linear Galois-equivariant period isomorphism α : H^j(𝔛_{K̄,tr},Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_st ≅ H^j_HK(𝔛) ⊗_F B_st preserving Frobenius and monodromy, and an induced filtered isomorphism α : H^j(𝔛_{K̄,tr},Q_p) ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR ≅ H^j_dR(𝔛_{K,tr}) ⊗_K B_dR. For r > j the map is the composite of α^FM_r (an isomorphism by Corollary 5.21) with the projections, and the proof proceeds as for Corollary 5.15 using the short exact sequences (5.24): the pair (H^j_HK(𝔛),H^j_dR(𝔛_{K,tr})) is a (ϕ,N)-filtered module with t_N = t_H, weakly admissible because V_st is finite dimensional, and V_st of it is H^j(𝔛_{K̄,tr},Q_p).
items.note: This is Corollary 1.10 of the introduction, whose second display prints ⊗_{Q_p} B_st where ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR is meant (source issue E2).

items.name: Remark 5.27: the fibre sequences lift to Banach Spaces
items.statement: The distinguished triangles (5.13) and (5.23) lift canonically to the category of finite dimensional Banach Spaces.
items.note: Attributed to reference [49], K-theory of log-schemes I (2008); the content described is that of [52], Geometric syntomic cohomology and vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve, which is in the bibliography but cited nowhere in the text (source issue E23).

items.name: Remark 5.28: the de Rham conjecture should follow
items.statement: It is likely that Scholze's de Rham conjecture for smooth proper rigid analytic spaces can be derived from Corollary 5.26 using Hartl's local semistable formal models of smooth rigid spaces and the gluing-on-the-generic-fibre techniques of Beilinson and Nekovář–Nizioł.
items.note: A speculation, not a theorem; recorded under gaps.

items.name: Cyclotomic monomials and commuting derivations before the decomposition
items.statement: For α∈{0,…,p−1}^{[0,d]}, set u_(cycl,α)=(1+T)^α_0 product_(j=1)^d X_j^α_j. Then ϕ_cycl(u_(cycl,α))=u_(cycl,α)^p. Define ∂_(cycl,0)=(1+T)∂/∂T and ∂_(cycl,j)=X_j∂/∂X_j for j≥1; the derivations commute and satisfy ∂_jϕ_cycl=pϕ_cycl∂_j. Their construction precedes the decomposition and does not use ψ.
items.note: Split from item 231 to remove the 231→232→241→231 cycle. No ψ operator is assumed when proving the decomposition.

routes.title: Cohomology comparisons: integral diagrams and rational period realizations, Part II: integral log-syntomic nearby cycles

Propose only the new integral logarithmic, quantitative nearby-cycle extension as a Part II. This is a rejected draft pending separation of existing CP.4 conclusions, supplier boundaries and recursive proof closure.
routes.brief: Final theorems, as the paper states them. (1) Theorem 1.1 = Theorem 5.4: for X a log-scheme with semistable reduction over O_K, or a base change of one over the ring of integers of a subfield, and 0 ≤ i ≤ r, the Fontaine–Messing period map α^FM_{r,n} : H^i(S_n(r)_X) → i^*R^ij_*Z/p^n(r)′_{X_tr} has kernel and cokernel annihilated by p^{Nr+c_p} when K has enough roots of unity (N universal, c_p depending only on p and, for p = 2, on d), and by p^N with N = N(K,p,r) in general. (2) Corollary 1.4 = Corollary 5.11: for i ≤ r−1 the composite α_{r,i} : H^{i−1}_dR(X_{K,tr}) → H^i_syn(X,r)_Q → H^i_ét(X_{K,tr},Q_p(r)) is an isomorphism, and α_{r,r} is injective with a cokernel that can be very large — a generalised Bloch–Kato exponential for quasi-compact semistable formal schemes. (3) Corollary 5.12: the geometric form over O_K̄, a p^{Nr}-quasi-isomorphism of sheaves for a universal N and, for proper log-smooth X, the isomorphism α^FM_r : H^j_syn(X_{O_K̄},r)_Q ≅ H^j(X_{tr,K̄},Q_p(r)) for j ≤ r. (4) Corollaries 5.15 and 5.26, the semistable conjecture for proper log-schemes of Cartier type and for proper semistable formal schemes: a natural B_st-linear Galois-equivariant period isomorphism H^j(X_{K̄,tr},Q_p) ⊗ B_st ≅ H^j_HK(X) ⊗_F B_st preserving ϕ and N, inducing a filtered isomorphism after ⊗B_dR. The following is a provisional inventory, not permission to reconstruct existing suppliers. What has to be built. (a) The integral log-syntomic package: the absolute log-crystalline complexes RΓ_cr(X,J^{[r]})_n over O_F, the syntomic complexes RΓ_syn(X,r)_n = [RΓ_cr(X,J^{[r]})_n --p^r−ϕ--> RΓ_cr(X_n)] with mapping fibres taken in the ∞-derived category, the sheaves J^{[r]}_{cr,n}, A_{cr,n} and S_n(r), the log-syntomic site of Remark 5.1 with its twists, and the geometric versions over O_K̄ (§§5.1.1, 5.1.7). (b) The local computation of §3: the Kummer complexes Kum(S,r) and their ψ-variants, the cyclotomic complex Cycl, the changes of disk and annulus of convergence (Proposition 3.3, Lemma 3.6, Corollary 3.9) and the change of Frobenius (Proposition 3.10) through the filtered Poincaré lemma of Lemma 3.11; the structural description of syntomic cohomology as a cone of a Hyodo–Kato over a de Rham term (Proposition 3.12) with the de Rham comparison of Lemma 3.14, Corollary 3.16 and Lemma 3.17, and the explicit computation for O^×_K (Proposition 3.19, which the authors state without proof and which a design job must therefore plan as an obligation). (c) The Fontaine–Messing period map of §4.7 and its identification with the Lazard-type map (Theorem 4.16), including the fat period ring E^PD_R and the Poincaré lemma it rests on. (d) The globalisation of §5.1: Abhyankar's lemma with Elkik approximation (Lemma 5.8), the K(π,1)-lemma for the trivialised locus of an affinoid (§5.1.4), the rigid GAGA comparison (§5.1.5), and the ramified Galois descent of Lemma 5.9 that removes the roots-of-unity hypothesis. (e) The Banach-Space argument of §5.2: Corollary 5.17, Lemma 5.19 — the variant of 'weakly admissible implies admissible' — and Proposition 5.20, together with the syntomic fibre sequences (5.13) and (5.23) and the short exact sequences they yield for j < r. Import the local (ϕ,Γ)-module comparison from route 2, the period rings from AInfCohomology AI.0 and PadicHodgeTheory R06.1, log geometry and Hyodo–Kato from CrystallineCohomology CR.5 and CR.6, Banach–Colmez theory from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB3, and the rigid-geometric inputs from ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1 and AdicEtaleGeometry A1. Do not plan the comparison with prismatic nearby cycles: PrismaticCohomology PR.4 proves a different statement (for a perfect base prism and a smooth formal scheme, with no constants), and the relation between the two is not in this paper. Do not plan Poincaré duality anywhere in the semistable comparison: the point of §5.2 is that the Banach-Space Dimension count replaces it, which is what makes the passage from schemes to formal schemes possible. REVIEW BOUNDARY: CP.4 already owns the overlapping proper flat semistable formal B_st comparison. Do not build that theorem again; separate the horizontal-boundary extension and map compatibility. D.2 is not a general log-syntomic supplier; Bloch–Kato maps are L1. E1 is rejected as an error claim; E22’s quantitative descent obligation remains. Lemma 3.17 is unfiltered (E28). This draft is not ready for design intake.

routes.title: (φ,Γ)-modules, Herr complexes and local Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: geometric toric towers
routes.reason: The parent roadmap builds the cyclotomic (phi,Gamma)-module theory over a p-adic field: the coefficient rings A_K and B_K, Fontaine's etale equivalence, overconvergence, Herr complexes, the psi operator and, at PG.7, the relative Robba category of Kedlaya-Pottharst-Xiao for affinoid families of Galois representations. This paper needs the relative theory in the arithmetic-geometric direction instead: rings built over a semistable affinoid with a log structure and a Kummer tower as well as a cyclotomic one, two Frobenii to be compared, an integral psi with its eigen-decomposition, Gamma_R = Gamma'_R semidirect Gamma_K, and a Koszul calculus with an integral Lazard isomorphism. That is the direction PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17 already proposed as PhiGammaModulesPartIIGeometricTowers - geometric toric towers, relative Robba rings at bounded radii, decompletion - so this extraction joins that id rather than opening a rival one, and says precisely what it adds: the logarithmic and semistable case, the Kummer tower, and the sections 2.6 and 4.2-4.5 machinery.
routes.brief: This joins the Part II proposed by PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17, whose brief covers geometric toric towers, relative Robba rings at bounded radii, weak and local decompletion and the exact tensor equivalence for globally étale modules. This paper adds the arithmetic-geometric, logarithmic and integral case that its Kummer tower requires, and a Koszul-complex calculus for it. Final theorems, as the paper states them. (1) Theorem 4.14: for R the p-adic completion of an étale algebra over O_F{X_1^{±1},…,X_a^{±1},X_{a+1},…,X_{d+1}}/(X_{d+1}X_{a+1}···X_{a+b} − ϖ) with the log structure of the divisor at infinity, and K with enough roots of unity, there are universal constants N and c_p and p^{Nr+c_p}-quasi-isomorphisms α^Laz_r : τ^{≤r}Syn(R,r) ≅ τ^{≤r}RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)) and its mod-p^n version. (2) Theorem 4.16: that map is p^{Nr+c_p}-equal to the Fontaine–Messing map. (3) Proposition 4.13: the relative Artin–Schreier sequence, almost étale descent and decompletion identify [RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_R(r)) --1−ϕ--> RΓ_cont(Γ_R,A_R(r))] with RΓ_cont(G_R,Z_p(r)). What has to be built. (a) The ring families of §2: the log-smooth lift R^+_ϖ of R over O_F with its PD envelope, the analytic rings R^{[u]}_ϖ, R^{[u,v]}_ϖ, R^{(0,v]+}_ϖ, R_ϖ and their one-variable models r^deco_ϖ, with the filtration by order of vanishing at X_0 = ϖ and the reduction R^deco_ϖ = r^deco_ϖ ⊗̂_{r^+_ϖ} R^+_ϖ; the implicit function theorem of Proposition 2.1 and the extension criterion of Proposition 2.12 that every later construction uses. (b) The two Frobenii and their left inverses: ϕ_Kum with ∂_{Kum,j}, ψ_Kum and the eigen-decomposition S = ⊕_αS_α (Lemmas 2.7–2.9), and the cyclotomic ϕ_cycl with ψ_cycl, its admissibility, the decomposition of Proposition 2.15 and the estimates of Proposition 2.16 including the constant ℓ_R and the p^{p+1}-isomorphism for the ψ = 0 part; the change of basis between the Kummer and cyclotomic monomials (Lemma 2.22) and the polycircle localisation argument it rests on (Lemmas 2.18–2.21). (c) The period rings and embeddings: the tilts and A_S, A^{(0,v]+}_S, A^{[u]}_S, A^{[u,v]}_S of §2.4 with their filtrations from B^+_dR(S), the comparison of A_cr with the annulus rings, the Artin–Schreier and fundamental exact sequences of Lemma 2.23, the Kummer and cyclotomic embeddings ι_Kum and ι_cycl (Proposition 2.31), the tower R_n with Γ_R = Γ′_R ⋊ Γ_K and its generators, the estimates of Lemmas 2.34 and 2.35, and the identity log γ_j = t∂_j. (d) The fat period rings SΛ⟨s⟩ of §2.6 with the structure theorem (Lemma 2.36), the filtered Poincaré lemma (Lemma 2.37), the rings E^PD_R, E^{[u,v]}_R, E^{[u,v]}_{R_∞}, E^{[u,v]}_R̄, their inclusions and the extension of ϕ and G_R to them (Lemmas 2.38–2.40), and the identification with Â_st in dimension 0. (e) The Koszul calculus of §4: the resolutions K(τ_1,…,τ_d), K(Λ) and K(Λ,τ) over the Iwasawa algebra, the group and Lie-algebra Koszul complexes and the Lazard–Mahler comparison λ, the integral Lazard isomorphism Laz = (β,β^c) of Lemma 4.6 with the convergence estimates that make ∇_j/τ_j invertible, the elimination of the filtration by powers of t (Lemma 4.4), and the changes of annulus and disk (Lemmas 4.8, 4.10, 4.12) through the ψ-complexes. Import the cyclotomic case from the parent roadmap PG.0–PG.5, the annulus rings from PadicHodgeTheory P7:annulus-foundations, the period rings from AInfCohomology AI.0 and PadicHodgeTheory R06.1, and almost purity from PerfectoidSpaces P3. Two cautions. The roots-of-unity hypothesis δ_R + 1 ≤ e_0/(2p) is not cosmetic: it is what gives the convergence inequality (1 + (p^{i−1}−δ_R−1)/e_0)u > 1/(p−1) used in Lemma 4.6, and a design job must carry it rather than assume the general case. And the truncation at degree r in Lemma 4.4 is unavoidable — multiplication by t^r is not a p^N-isomorphism in degrees ≥ r+1 for any N — so no layer may state the comparison without it. Reuse TopRep.homogeneousCochains and the upstream ProfiniteCohomology carrier; ArithmeticGaloisDuality owns its compact/derived extension. The generic Koszul supplier must serve this geometric tower, derived/prismatic comparisons and deformation/patching consumers once. A name match to Koszul signs is insufficient. Recompute downstream numerical filtration losses after E26.

gaps.detail: Proposition 3.19, the explicit computation of the syntomic cohomology of O^×_K (H^0 is p^{13r}-trivial, H^1 is p^{N(r,e)}-isomorphic to O^{(r)}_K, plus an extra Z_p and a term O_F/(ϕ−1) when r = 1), is stated by the authors without proof — 'We will state the following proposition without a proof' — and is not attributed to any other paper. A design job must plan it as an obligation of its own, not import it. It matters because Remark 3.18 uses it to show that the syntomic exponential α_{r,r} of Corollary 3.16 is not surjective.

Three statements in the paper are expectations and must not be planned as results. Remark 1.7: the descent of §5.1 would remove the roots-of-unity hypothesis from Theorem 1.6 at the cost of constants depending on K, and 'it seems likely' that they could be made to depend only on the valuation of the different; the same remark expects an analogue of Corollary 1.4 for a general affinoid smooth in characteristic 0, with constants depending on the p-adic valuation of suitable Jacobians. Remark 5.28: it is 'likely' that Scholze's de Rham conjecture for smooth proper rigid spaces can be derived from Corollary 5.26 using Hartl's local semistable models and the gluing techniques of Beilinson and Nekovář–Nizioł. And §2.2.6 records that one could perhaps use Breuil–Kisin or Caruso's (ϕ,τ)-modules, and hence ϕ_Kum throughout, instead of (ϕ,Γ)-modules and ϕ_cycl — a route this paper does not take.

Track every bound by parameter. E1 is rejected: weaker N(K,p,r) is not a contradiction of N(e,p,r). E22 records the unclosed relative descent estimate with corrected scalar transcription and K_0 meaning. E16 is a proof gap for p^8; p^(2(p+7)) follows safely. E9 needs integer rounding and E11 removes undefined c_e. None of these estimates is advertised as sharp.

§1.2.3 sets up the bracket notation as a homotopy limit and records that the squares involved are strictly commutative — so that the bracket is the total complex of a double complex — 'everywhere but in Section 5'. A formalisation of §5 must therefore use genuine homotopy limits in the ∞-derived category, which is also how the mapping fibres of §5.1.1 are defined; replacing them by total complexes would change the statements.

Corollary 5.21’s proof passes through finite coefficients before rationalization. The first/second/final-claim wording does not establish that a theorem was accidentally omitted. Prove the formal local-to-global comparison and the finite-coefficient/derived-limit transition explicitly.

The atlas plans p-adic nearby cycles as Frobenius fixed points of prismatic cohomology at PrismaticCohomology PR.4, for a perfect base prism and a smooth formal scheme, with no constants. That is a different statement from this paper's, which is logarithmic, semistable, integral and only true up to universal constants, and the two are not compared here. A design job must not import one for the other, and a link between the two layers has to be proved rather than assumed.

The hypothesis that K contains enough roots of unity, δ_K + [K:F_{i(K)}] < e/(2p), is used in two distinct ways: qualitatively, to have the field-of-norms element π_K and hence the cyclotomic embedding ι_cycl and the Γ_R-action on the syntomic complexes at all; and quantitatively, through δ_R + 1 ≤ e_0/(2p), to make the series defining ∇_j/τ_j converge in Lemma 4.6 and the estimates of Lemmas 2.34, 2.35 and 2.38 hold. A layer that states the local comparison must carry the hypothesis in the quantitative form; the general case is only reached by the descent of §5.1, with a constant depending on K.

The truncation at degree r is not a convenience. In Lemma 4.4 multiplication by t^r is a p^{4r}-isomorphism in degrees ≤ r but is not a p^N-isomorphism in degrees ≥ r+1 for any N, which is why the main theorems are stated for τ^{≤r}; in Lemma 3.6 and Corollary 3.9 the constants in degrees > r are merely too large (Remark 3.8 notes that truncating there is avoidable at the cost of constants involving log e). A design job must keep the two reasons distinct and must not state an untruncated comparison.

Supply constructors, extensionality, functoriality, coefficient maps, hypotheses, integral/rational transitions and non-vacuous tests derived from actual consumers for each item.

In particular items 119 and 251 now make completion and the relative spectral valuation function explicit, and Lemma 2.23’s full fundamental kernel needs the twist normalization.

All ten route drafts require the precise changes recorded in the independent route verdicts. A source route cannot expand a narrow stage by calling a broader statement planned. CP.4 already includes formal semistable comparison; use it once. Join the Liu–Zhu geometric-tower proposal instead of creating a duplicate design.
